Title: "Interview: Living Abroad"
Text:
"Interview: Living Abroad
Image

Are you hesitant about studying college abroad? Curious about life overseas? Individuals from China, England, Pakistan, the Philippines, Russia, Scotland, Serbia, Slovakia, South Africa, the United Kingdom, and the United States who have lived abroad share their insights and experiences to broaden your perspective on living away from your native country.

你还在犹豫是否要出国上大学吗？你想知道在国外生活是什么样的吗？曾经在中国、英国、巴基斯坦、菲律宾、俄罗斯、苏格兰、塞尔维亚、斯洛伐克、南非、英国和美国生活过的人提供了他们的见解和经验，以拓宽你对远离自己国家生活的看法。 

These participants have lived in countries such as Canada, China, France, Germany, Montenegro, South America, the United Arab Emirates, and the USA, many for over five years. They describe living abroad as a transformative experience that enriches your life. You'll learn about different people, cultures, and life perspectives, fostering personal growth, confidence, and independence.

他们曾居住在加拿大、中国、法国、德国、黑山、南美洲、阿拉伯联合酋长国和美国等国家，大多超过五年。他们说，在国外生活是一次奇妙的经历，它会改变你的生活。你可以学到很多关于不同的人、文化和生活观点的知识，还可以进一步发展自己，获得自信或独立。

ImageImage

However, living abroad comes with challenges. These include language barriers, culture shock, interactions with locals, discrimination, and adjusting to different lifestyles. Initially, language barriers can be daunting, but with time, you'll start picking up the language, immersing yourself in the culture and studying the language to help connect with locals and peers. Culture shock may lead to misunderstandings due to unfamiliar customs and beliefs; patience and adaptability are keys to overcoming these differences. Bad situations with locals may also arise, one interviewee experienced being “treated as a dollar bill,” locals would try to make money off of him with scams. Discrimination was mainly an issue faced by students. The best thing to do is to ignore the marks made against you. 

然而，在国外生活也面临着挑战。其中包括语言障碍、文化冲击、与当地人的互动、歧视以及适应不同的生活方式。最初，语言障碍可能令人望而生畏，但随着时间你会慢慢适应新的语言，让自己沉浸在文化中并学习语言，以帮助与当地人和同龄人建立联系。文化冲击可能会因不熟悉的习俗和信仰而导致误解；耐心和适应是克服这些差异的关键。与当地人的关系也可能会出现不好的情况，一位受访者经历了“被当作美元钞票”，当地人会试图通过诈骗从他身上赚钱。歧视是学生经常会面临的问题。最好的办法就是忽略那些针对你的歧视。

ImageImage

Ways of living like work hours, essentials and social interactions will also be very different and can be hard to get used to at first. A student highlighted that the schedule was more packed abroad compared to his native country so he struggles with keeping up with the schedule. A way he has been dealing with this is by improving his sleep schedule. Acquiring familiar daily products and foods can be challenging initially, but integrating into the local community and trying popular local items can ease this transition. Socially, integrating into friend groups and building relationships may require stepping out of your comfort zone, initiating small talk, and gradually establishing connections.

工作时间、生活必需品和社交互动等生活方式也将大不相同，一开始可能很难适应。一名学生强调，与他的国家相比，国外的日程安排更加紧凑，因此他很难跟上日程安排。他处理这个问题的一种方法是改善他的睡眠时间表。获得熟悉的日常产品和食物最初可能会很困难，但融入当地社区并尝试流行的当地物品可以缓解这种转变。在社交方面，融入朋友群体并建立关系可能需要走出你的舒适区，一开始从闲聊，并逐渐建立联系。

ImageImage

In conclusion, to prepare for living abroad, interviewees recommend several steps. First, learning the language enhances your ability to interact with locals. Second, thorough research on practical matters like housing and budgeting, as well as understanding local laws and customs, is crucial. Different countries have varying social norms and taboos, so familiarizing yourself beforehand can prevent misunderstandings. Lastly, mentally preparing yourself for unexpected challenges and reinforcing your reasons for choosing a particular country are essential for a successful experience abroad.

总之，为了准备出国生活，受访者建议采取以下几个步骤。首先，学习语言可以增强与当地人互动的能力。其次，对房租和预算等实际问题进行深入研究以及了解当地法律和习俗至关重要。不同国家有不同的社会规范和禁忌，因此事先熟悉可以防止遇到误解。最后，为意想不到的挑战做好心理准备，并强化选择特定国家的理由，对于在国外获得成功的经历至关重要。

With the start of the school year and the continuous expansion of our newsletter organization, we are looking to recruit more members who are interested in joining Polarity, the student paper. If you are interesed in joining Polarity as a writer, editor, translator, artist or photographer, please scan the QR code on the poster and contact our editors-in-chief. 

随着新学年的开始和我们的学生新闻社的持续扩展，我们正在寻找更多有兴趣加入报社Polarity。如果你想以编辑、特约撰稿人、设计师、平台运营者或摄影师的身份加入Polarity，请扫描海报里的二维码并联系主编。

Polarity, founded on July 17, 2022, is a student-runned paper that aims to give students a platform to write about their interests and “make their voices heard.” Over 60 articles about various topics such as news, editorials, popular science articles, book/movie reviews, trend stories, interviews, and more have been published. This was made possible by our team of faculty advisors, editors-in-chief, writers, editors, translators, artists, photographers and platform operators. Throughout the years, we have recruited around 30 students who share an interest in writing and publishing articles to express their personal opinions and hobbies.

Polarity成立于2022年7月17日，是一份由学生主办的报纸，旨在为学生们提供一个平台，让他们能够写下自己的兴趣并“发出自己的声音”。截至目前，我们已发布了60多篇关于新闻、社论、科普文章、书籍/电影评论、趋势故事、访谈等各种主题的文章。这一切都得益于我们的教职员工顾问、编辑主任、作家、编辑、翻译、艺术家、摄影师以及平台运营者。多年来，我们已招募了约30名对写作和发表文章感兴趣的学生，他们通过这些文章表达个人观点和爱好。

Title: "Future is Never Decided by One Moment 未来从不由一刻决定"
Text:
"Future is Never Decided by One Moment 未来从不由一刻决定
Image

As exam scores approach—or perhaps they've already been released by the time you read this—many people are likely to feel frustrated with themselves, regardless of their results. You might be upset about misreading a question or failing to study a minor topic that appeared on the test. These issues may seem like the sole reasons for a disappointing grade. Had we been more attentive during the test, we might have achieved our ideal score and enjoyed a brief period of happiness.

当考试成绩临近，或者当你阅读这段话时成绩已经公布时，许多人可能会对自己感到沮丧，不论结果如何。你可能会因为误解了一个问题或没能复习到一个在考试中出现的小话题而感到不满。这些问题可能看起来是令人失望的成绩的唯一原因。如果我们在考试中更专注一些，也许我们能取得理想的分数，并短暂地感到快乐。

But is that true? To blame a single moment for our current distress? If we could go back in time, would correcting that one error be the only change needed?

但这真的是真的吗？把我们当前的困扰归咎于某一瞬间？如果我们能回到过去，纠正那个错误是否就是唯一需要的改变？

Think about it. Would you have made the careless mistake if you didn’t have to spend all your brainpower on figuring out the question? If you had practiced more and been more familiar with those types of questions, you could have directed your focus to making fewer of these simple mistakes.

想一想。如果你没把所有的脑力都花在弄清楚问题上，你会犯那个粗心的错误吗？如果你多加练习，对这些问题类型更加熟悉，你可能能将注意力集中在减少这些简单错误上。

If you had been genuinely interested in and curious about the subject, you might have explored it more thoroughly on your own. Compare this approach with attempting to achieve high scores with the least effort possible, generally, which one leads to better outcomes?

如果你对这个科目真的感兴趣并充满好奇，你可能会自己更深入地探索它。把这种方法与尽量少花力气去获得高分的方式相比，通常哪种方式会带来更好的结果？

We tend to overestimate and overemphasize how pivotal one point in our lives is. We put all the blame or credit on the decisions and actions made in that one moment. The reality is that anything that happened to us is just as pivotal as the series of events that led to it and the series of events that followed it. An exam wouldn’t have caught you off guard if you were well-prepared. You could have been prepared if you hadn't crammed at the last minute. Last-minute cramming happens if you procrastinate, which occurs if you lack interest or understanding of the subject. Understanding the subject requires paying attention in class, which is difficult if you’re exhausted from staying up late.

我们往往高估了生活中的一个瞬间有多么关键。我们将所有的责任或功劳都归结于那一刻的决定和行动。现实是，发生在我们身上的任何事情都与导致它的事件系列和随后的事件系列同样重要。如果你准备的很充分，考试不会让你措手不及。如果你没有临时抱佛脚，你可能已经做好了准备。临时抱佛脚的情况发生在你拖延时，而拖延发生在你对科目缺乏兴趣或理解。理解这个科目需要在课堂上认真听讲，如果你因为熬夜而疲惫不堪，这就很难做到了。

The main point of all of this is that we shouldn’t be down on ourselves because of that one mistake we made. Instead, we should reflect on all the actions and inactions that led to it. What values, beliefs, and attitudes led us to make those decisions, and can we still keep them going forward if they continue to interfere with our goals? Is there anything that we can do to minimize the effects of the mistakes we already made? Focus on what can be changed rather than what cannot.

所有这些的主要观点是，我们不应该因为一个错误而对自己感到沮丧。相反，我们应该反思导致这个错误的所有行动和不作为。是什么样的价值观、信念和态度促使我们做出了那些决定？如果这些继续干扰我们的目标，我们还能继续坚持这些价值观吗？我们能做些什么来最小化已经犯下的错误的影响？专注于可以改变的事情，而不是不能改变的事情。

If, after reflection, you still don’t enjoy the subject and prefer minimal effort, that’s fine. Just be realistic about what you can achieve with that mindset. However, don’t be afraid to dream big and work hard.

如果在反思之后，你仍然不喜欢这个科目，且更倾向于最小化努力，那也没关系。只是要现实地看待在这种心态下你能实现什么。然而，不要害怕梦想大，并努力去实现。

Regardless of your decision, be kind to your past self. You did your best at that moment and that’s something to be proud of.

无论你做出什么决定，都要对过去的自己保持善意。那时候你已经尽力了，这是值得自豪的。

Title: "Feminism in the 2024 Olympics: A Milestone for Gender Equality"
Text:
"Feminism in the 2024 Olympics: A Milestone for Gender Equality
Image

The 2024 Paris Summer Olympics represent a historic milestone in the pursuit of gender equality in sports. For the first time in Olympic history, the games will achieve full gender parity, with an equal number of female and male athletes. Out of 10,500 athletes, 5,250 are expected to be women. This achievement results from years of sustained efforts by the International Olympic Committee and various stakeholders promoting gender equality in sports.

2024年巴黎夏季奥运会标志着体育领域性别平等追求的历史性里程碑。这是奥运历史上首次实现性别完全平衡，女性和男性运动员的数量相等。预计在10500名运动员中，有5250名将是女性。这一成就得益于国际奥委会和各方利益相关者多年持续推动体育领域性别平等的努力。

The journey toward gender parity at the Olympics has been long and challenging. Women first participated in the Olympics in 1900, representing just 2.2% of all athletes and competing in only a few events such as golf and tennis. Over the years, women’s representation has steadily increased. Notably, the London 2012 Olympics marked a significant step forward as the first games where every participating nation included female athletes in their delegations. By the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, women’s participation reached approximately 48%, paving the way for full parity achieved in Paris.

实现奥运会性别平衡的旅程漫长而艰辛。女性于1900年首次参加奥运会，当时仅占所有运动员的2.2%，并仅在高尔夫和网球等少数项目中比赛。多年来，女性的代表性稳步增加。值得注意的是，2012年伦敦奥运会是第一个每个参赛国家都包括女性运动员的比赛。到2020年东京奥运会时，女性的参与率达到了大约48%，为巴黎的全面平衡铺平了道路。

At the opening ceremony of the Paris Olympic Games, a symbolic moment unfolded on the banks of the Seine River. Ten golden female statues began to rise sequentially from the water, accompanied by a stirring rendition of “La Marseillaise” sung by a female vocalist from a rooftop. This segment, named “SORORITÉ” (Female Friendship), honored ten eminent French women: Olympe de Gouges, Alice Milliat, Gisèle Halimi, Simone de Beauvoir, Paulette Nardal, Jeanne Barret, Louise Michel, Christine de Pizan, Alice Guy, and Simone Veil.

在巴黎奥运会的开幕式上，塞纳河畔上演了一个象征性的时刻。十座金色女性雕像依次从水中升起，同时伴随着女歌手在屋顶上演唱的《马赛曲》。这个环节名为“姐妹情”（SORORITÉ），旨在致敬十位杰出的法国女性：奥林匹亚·德·古热、爱丽丝·米利亚、吉赛尔·哈利米、西蒙娜·德·波伏娃、波莱特·纳达尔、让娜·巴雷、路易丝·米歇尔、克里斯蒂娜·德·皮赞、爱丽丝·盖和西蒙娜·韦伊。

However, due to a mechanical issue, only nine of the statues emerged, with Simone de Beauvoir’s statue remaining submerged. This absence served as a poignant reminder of her significant impact and enduring legacy, underscoring that while progress has been made, much work remains in the pursuit of gender equality and recognition.

然而，由于机械故障，只有九座雕像升起，西蒙娜·德·波伏娃的雕像仍然沉没。这一缺失成为她重大影响力和持久遗产的深刻提醒，强调了尽管取得了进展，但在性别平等和认可的追求中仍有许多工作要做。

Achieving gender parity at the Olympics is seen as a crucial step toward broader societal changes. According to the World Economic Forum’s Global Gender Gap Report 2023, the global gender gap is only 68.4% closed, and at the current rate, complete gender equality might not be achieved for another 131 years. The visibility and success of female athletes at such a prestigious global event can inspire further progress in leadership, education, and economic participation.

实现奥运会的性别平衡被视为更广泛社会变革的重要一步。根据世界经济论坛2023年全球性别差距报告，全球性别差距仅关闭68.4%，以当前的速度，完全性别平等可能还需要131年才能实现。女性运动员在这一享有盛誉的全球盛会上的可见性和成功，可以激励其他领域的进一步进展，包括领导力、教育和经济参与。

In conclusion, the 2024 Paris Olympics mark a historic achievement for gender equality in sports. As the world watches, these games will celebrate athletic prowess and symbolize the ongoing struggle and progress toward equal representation and opportunity for all genders in every sphere of life.

总之，2024年巴黎奥运会是体育领域性别平等的历史性成就。当全世界注视时，这场比赛不仅将庆祝运动能力，还将象征着在各个生活领域中为所有性别争取平等代表和机会的持续斗争和进展。

Title: "Living a Thousand Days vs Living One Day a Thousand Times"
Text:
"Living a Thousand Days vs Living One Day a Thousand Times
Image

There is a difference between living a thousand days and living one day a thousand times. I’m sure we all get bored of meaningless repetition and would rather do the former than the latter. However, the reality is that most of us are stuck spending weeks and months on end following the same daily routine, doing the same activities, and going to bed worrying about the same thing. Most of this is because of all the seemingly endless responsibilities put onto us for us to fulfill. So how do we live each day differently? How do we do this and not get overwhelmed by our responsibilities?

生活一千天和活一天一千次是有区别的。我相信我们都会对无意义的重复感到厌烦，更愿意选择前者而不是后者。然而，现实是大多数人都困在相同的日常生活中，周而复始地过着相同的日子，做着相同的事情，晚上担心着相同的问题。这大多是因为我们肩负着无穷无尽的责任，而这些责任看似永无止境。那么，如何让我们每天都过得不同？如何做到这一点，同时又不被责任压得喘不过气？

The key to “living a thousand days” is to do things that are meaningful and enjoyable to you every day. They don’t have to be big things. It could be working for something that you are passionate about. It could be playing this random game you found that you find fun. It could be spending time with someone you like. Whatever it is, find at least a few minutes a day to do it. As long as it gives you a sense of fulfillment and happiness, it can make life meaningful and feel less repetitive. One thing that it shouldn’t be is a burden. Make sure that you always have the choice to not do it if you don’t feel like doing it that day. Otherwise, it just becomes another responsibility.

“活出一千天”的关键是每天都做一些对你来说有意义且令人愉悦的事情。它们不必是大事。它可以是为你所热衷的事情而努力。它可以是玩一个你偶然发现并觉得有趣的游戏。它可以是和你喜欢的人共度时光。不论是什么，确保每天至少花几分钟去做这些事情。只要它能给你带来满足感和幸福感，它就能让生活变得有意义，不那么重复。而一件事情不应该成为负担。确保你总是有选择不做的权利，如果那天你不想做它的话。否则，它就会变成另一个责任。

Try out new things that interest you and don’t be afraid to stop doing things that don’t interest you anymore. What you find meaningful and fulfilling now doesn’t have to be the same as what made you fulfilled the day before. Just make sure that there is something to look forward to. If you wake up every day dreading the things that are to come, then you are living your life wrong.

尝试新的让你感兴趣的事情，不要害怕停止做那些你已经不再感兴趣的事情。你现在觉得有意义和满足的事情，不一定要和前一天让你感到满足的事情相同。只要确保每天都有一些值得期待的事情。如果你每天醒来时都在害怕接下来要发生的事情，那说明你生活得不对。

A common mistake is thinking that it is fine to reserve time for meaningful fun for until after all your responsibilities have been accomplished. There isn’t enough time for that. Life nowadays is extremely fast-paced. In high school, weekends are filled with homework, preparation for exams, and programs for well-rounded development. The moment high school is over, you are preparing for university. The moment university is over, you are preparing for work. By the time work is over, you are already over 60 years old and likely still have a lot of responsibilities like taking care of your grandchildren or repaying the debt you owe. Not only that, but you also are likely facing a myriad of health issues from all the stress you’ve been through.

一个常见的错误是认为在完成所有责任之后再去留出时间享受有意义的乐趣是没问题的。但事实是没有那么多时间。现在的生活节奏非常快。在高中时，周末都充满了作业、备考和全面发展的各种项目。高中一结束，你就在为大学做准备。大学一结束，你又在为工作做准备。等工作结束时，你已经超过60岁了，而且很可能还要承担很多责任，比如照顾孙辈或偿还债务。不仅如此，你还可能因为长期承受的压力而面临各种健康问题。

But doesn’t having fun this way distract our focus on what is “really important” and limit our potential, leading to our inevitable doom?

但是，以这种方式享乐会不会分散我们对“真正重要”事情的注意力，限制我们的潜力，最终导致不可避免的失败呢？

The answer is no.

答案是否定的。

Having fun has been scientifically proven to increase productivity. Having fun when done right actually increases our potential instead of limiting it. But there is a catch to it. One, you must be in control. If you aren’t able to decide when to have fun and when to stop having fun, you may get carried away, leading to having not enough time to fulfill your responsibilities. The second is that fun shouldn’t be an avoidance strategy. What must be done still has to be done.

科学已经证明，享乐可以提高生产力。如果适度享乐，实际上是提高我们的潜力，而不是限制它。但这里有一个关键点。首先，你必须掌控好自己。如果你不能决定什么时候该享乐，什么时候该停止，那么你可能会过度沉迷，导致没有足够的时间履行你的责任。其次，享乐不应该成为逃避责任的策略。该做的事情仍然必须完成。

At the end of the day, most of us don’t find studies and work meaningful. However, they are important because they buy time for us to do things that are.

归根结底，大多数人不会觉得学习和工作有多么有意义。然而，它们很重要，因为它们为我们争取到了做有意义事情的时间。

Title: "ABOUT POLARITY (S.Y. 2024-2025) | 社团&成员介绍"
Text:
"ABOUT POLARITY (S.Y. 2024-2025) | 社团&成员介绍
Image

Polarity Introduction (Polarity 介绍)

Polarity (motto: "Fortress of Diversity") is Chiway Repton School Xiamen's first student-run publication with a goal of providing students a platform to “make their voices heard." Polarity was founded on July 17, 2022 but went on a hiatus and officially relaunched on January 15, 2024. Polarity currently has 24 members, including a faculty advisor, editors-in-chief, editors, staff writers, designers, platform operators, and photographers. The word “Polarity” is implicitly connected to the two poles, the Arctic and Antarctic, choosing it as the name of our publication symbolizes our commitment to embracing a wide range of opinions and perspectives.

《Polarity》（座右铭：“多样性的堡垒”）是厦门华锐莱普顿学校第一本学生自办的刊物，旨在为学生提供一个“让自己的声音被听到”的平台。《Polarity》成立于 2022 年 7 月 17 日，但后来中断了， 2024年1月15日正式重新上线。Polarity目前有24名成员，包括导师、主编、编辑、特约撰稿人、设计师、平台运营者、摄影师。“Polarity”这个词隐含着两个极点， 北极和南极，选择它作为我们出版物的名称象征着我们致力于包容广泛的意见和观点。

Image

We mainly operate on two platforms, our WeChat subscription account and our official website, and have published many kinds of articles varying from news, editorials, popular science articles, and film reviews to art reviews, poems, flash fiction, and original stories. This year, our special columns include: Narrative Nook for original stories and film/book reviews, Dialogue Digest for student interviews and advice, and Birthday Bulletin for commemorating a member’s special day. These columns are managed by students who specialize in these fields.

我们主要运营微信订阅号和官方网站两个平台，发表新闻、社论、科普文章、影评、艺术评论、诗歌、短篇小说、原创故事等多种类型的文章。 今年，我们的特别专栏包括：用于原创故事和电影/书评的叙事角落，用于学生采访和建议的对话文摘，以及用于纪念会员特殊日子的生日公告。 这些专栏由专门研究这些领域的学生管理。

Title: "Paradox of Freedom 自由的悖论"
Text:
"Paradox of Freedom 自由的悖论
Image

Freedom is a concept that has been debated for centuries, and its meaning can often seem elusive. In my dream, I saw a monarchy that clearly did not advocate for equality. This thought lingered in my mind even after I woke up, and it led me to question whether any system of governance truly supports equality in power. From what I’ve reflected on, it seems that all forms of governance inevitably fall short in achieving true equality. Monarchy, democracy, communism—each places power in the hands of some, not all. The only system that seems to offer true equality in power is anarchy, though even that presents its own challenges.

自由是一个争论了几个世纪的概念，它的含义往往看起来难以捉摸。在我的梦中，我看到了一个明显不提倡平等的君主制。这个想法在我醒来后仍然萦绕在我的脑海中，它让我质疑是否有任何治理制度真正支持权力平等。从我的反思来看，似乎所有形式的治理都不可避免地实现真正的平等。君主制、民主制、共产主义——每一种都把权力交给了一部分人，而不是所有人。似乎唯一能提供真正权力平等的制度是无政府状态，尽管这也有其自身的挑战。

Many leaders claim to advocate for freedom, but what does freedom really mean? I believe that freedom is inherently limited. In the society we live in, we cannot do everything we desire because we share this world with others. In order to avoid harming one another and maintain a stable society, we have established laws and rules. However, these laws, while necessary for order, also restrict our individual freedom.

许多领导人声称主张自由，但自由的真正含义是什么?我相信自由本质上是有限的。在我们生活的社会里，我们不能随心所欲，因为我们与他人共享这个世界。为了避免彼此伤害，维护社会稳定，我们制定了法律和规则。然而，这些法律虽然是维持秩序所必需的，但也限制了我们的个人自由。

Beyond laws, there are unspoken rules that govern how we interact with others, especially in social situations. These norms dictate what is acceptable and what is not. If we fail to conform, we risk being excluded from social groups. So, while we strive for freedom, we are constantly negotiating with limitations—both legal and social.

除了法律之外，还有一些潜规则支配着我们如何与他人互动，尤其是在社交场合。这些规范规定了什么是可被接受的，什么是不可被接受的。如果我们不能随波逐流，我们就有被社会群体排斥的风险。因此，当我们为自由而奋斗时，我们也在不断地与法律和社会的限制进行磋商。

True, unrestricted freedom may be impossible to achieve. But in this pursuit, we can maximize the freedom we do have by choosing who to support, what to believe in, and how to live our lives. In a world full of restrictions, it’s important to remember that freedom lies not only in the absence of rules but in the choices we make within them.

说真的，不受限制的自由可能是不可能实现的。但在这种追求中，我们可以通过选择支持谁、相信谁以及如何生活，来最大限度地发挥我们所拥有的自由。在一个充满限制的世界里，重要的是要记住，自由不是在于没有规则，而在于我们在规则范围内做出的选择。

In the end, freedom may not be an absolute state, but it is something we can continually strive to expand in meaningful ways. We may never have complete freedom, but we can work to protect and maximize the liberties that allow us to live authentically and meaningfully in society.

最后，自由可能不是一种绝对开放的状态，但它是我们可以不断努力以有意义的方式扩大的东西。我们可能永远不会拥有完全的自由，但我们可以努力保护和最大化自由，使我们能够在社会中真实而有意义地生活。

Title: "如何提升人生幸福感 How to Enhance Life Satisfaction"
Text:
"如何提升人生幸福感 How to Enhance Life Satisfaction
Image

什么会让你感到幸福？取得一个重大成就、胜利，亦或享有某种财富，就能让你体验到幸福吗？在大卫·斯坦德·拉斯特这个热门的TED演讲动画版中，大卫解释说简单调整你的日常行为，可能就会改变你的所见、所感和所为。

What makes you feel truly happy? Is it achieving a major goal, winning or acquiring wealth? In his popular TED talk animation, David Steindl-Rast explains that simply adjusting your daily actions can change how you see, feel and act.

他指出，幸福感与感恩紧密相关，即使拥有幸福的人也可能因不知足而缺乏感恩，而经历不幸的人仍可能感到快乐，因为他们心怀感激。

He emphasizes that happiness is deeply connected to gratitude. Even those who seem to have everything may feel unhappy because they are not grateful, while those who face difficulties can still feel joy if they cultivate gratitude.

那么，我们所说的感恩到底是什么？它又从何而来呢？感恩如同我们得到某件至宝，而且它是被赐予的。这两点必须结合起来，它必须是珍贵的东西，而且是份真正的礼物。当这两点同时具备时，感恩之情就会在心里油然而生，而幸福感也会如影随形，感恩之情就是这样产生的。这一切的关键在于我们不能只是偶尔体验感恩，我们要成为生活在感恩中的人。

So, what exactly is gratitude? Where does it come from? Gratitude arises when we receive something valuable — a genuine gift. Both conditions must exist: the gift must be precious and freely given. When these two factors are met, a sense of gratitude naturally arises and happiness follows closely behind. This highlights the importance of not merely experiencing gratitude occasionally but striving to live with gratitude.

为了活在感恩中，我们应该体验每个时刻作为天赐和礼物，珍惜当下和其中的契机。我们不必对一切感恩，但可以对每个时刻的机会心存感激，即使在极端困境中也要抓住机会。

To live in gratitude, we must treat every moment as a gift and cherish the opportunities it presents. We don’t have to feel grateful for every situation but we can appreciate the opportunities in each moment, even in challenging circumstances.

那么，如何找到一种方法能让我们生活在感恩中，不是偶尔，而是时刻心存感激地生活呢？我们怎样才能做到这一点？有种很简单的方法：停、看、行。

How can we cultivate a way of life that isn’t just occasionally grateful, but consistently full of appreciation? The answer is simple: Stop, Look and Go.

1. 停：我们匆匆走过人生，从不止步，因此错过机遇。我们得停下来，沉静片刻，感受美好。

2. 看：开启所有感官，享受天赐。

3. 行：拥抱机会，付诸行动。

1. Stop: We often rush through life without passing, missing opportunities to experience gratitude.

2. Look: Open your senses and enjoy the beauty and blessings that life offers.

3. Go: Seize the opportunity and act on it.

感恩的浪潮能够改变世界，因为感恩带来无畏、非暴力、分享和尊重差异，从而改变权力结构。构建一个由小团体构成的网络，成员间相互认识和互动，可以形成一个充满感恩的世界。

Gratitude has the potential to change the world. It fosters courage, non-violence, sharing and respect for differences, challenging traditional power structures. Building networks of small, connected communities where people know and interact with each other can create a world full of gratitude and happiness.

Written By: Christine Liu

Title: "The Queen of Mystery 推理女王"
Text:
"The Queen of Mystery 推理女王
ImageImage

Agatha Christie is considered the best-selling novelist of all time, with over 4 billion copies of her works sold globally. What made Agatha Christie such a successful writer was her compelling and skillful writing style, attracting readers for over 60 years. This article analyzes key elements of Agatha Christie’s writing style through her most iconic characters and the structure of the story. From her mastery of characterization to complicated plotting techniques, Christie established the map for classic Golden Age British murder mysteries.

阿加莎·克里斯蒂被认为是有史以来销量最高的小说家，全球销售作品超过40亿本。她的成功归因于她引人入胜且技巧高超的写作风格，吸引了读者超过60年。本文分析了阿加莎·克里斯蒂写作风格的关键元素，探讨她最具标志性的角色和故事结构。从她对人物刻画的精湛技巧到复杂的情节构建，克里斯蒂为经典黄金时代英国谋杀悬疑小说奠定了基础。

One of Agatha Christie’s writing styles was her ability to craft memorable, multilayered characters. The most famous two characters for decades are the eccentric Belgian detective Hercule Poirot and old spinster Miss Jane Marple.

阿加莎·克里斯蒂的写作风格之一是她能够塑造令人难忘、层次丰富的人物。在几十年里，最著名的两个角色是古怪的比利时侦探赫尔克里·波洛和老处女简·马普尔小姐。

Poirot made his first appearance in 1920’s The Mysterious Affair at Styles. With his egg-shaped head and curious mustache, Poirot is meticulous in his observations and reasoning. As a former Belgian police inspector, he is very proud of his work, occasionally coming across as vain or arrogant. However, beneath his obsession with order is a strong compassion for victims.

波洛首次出现在1920年的《斯泰尔斯的神秘事件》中。他那蛋形的头部和好奇的胡子使他十分显眼。作为一名前比利时警察，他在观察和推理方面非常细致。波洛对自己的工作感到非常自豪，有时显得有些自负或傲慢。然而，在他对秩序的执着之下，实际上蕴藏着对受害者的深切同情。

Miss Marple first appeared in 1930’s Murder at the Vicarage. A gossiping old biddy on the surface, Miss Marple possesses a penetrating understanding of human nature through observation of her small English village. During tea parties with the locals, she gathers crumbs of information later pieced together into important insights.

马普尔小姐首次出现在1930年的《牧师公馆谋杀案》中。表面上看，她是一位爱说闲话的老小姐，但通过对她小小英格兰村庄的观察，马普尔小姐对人性有着深刻的理解。在与当地人举行的茶会上，她收集一些信息的碎片，随后将这些信息拼凑成重要的洞见。

According to her autobiography, Agatha Christie usually began her writing process by devising the core elements of the mystery – the murder method and the killer’s identity and motives. She then wrote the story with a combination of seemingly reasonable suspects to mislead readers. Christie took great care in constructing puzzle-like plots with multiple layered clues that built towards the climactic revealing of who had “done it.”

根据她的自传，阿加莎·克里斯蒂通常在写作过程中首先构思出谜团的核心要素——谋杀手法以及凶手的身份和动机。接着，她会结合看似合理的嫌疑人来误导读者。克里斯蒂非常用心地构建类似谜题的情节，设下多层线索，最终揭示出“真相”。

Many of Christie’s novels follow a formulaic structure that effectively builds suspense. An initial discovery of a crime is followed by a police investigation interviewing all suspects. Throughout, Christie releases clues that alternately implicate and clear different suspects in the reader’s mind. Just as the reader believes they have solved it, Christie introduces plot twists like alibis or new facts that reverse expectations. Interpersonal tensions and red herrings also help to confuse the trail until the final resolution.

克里斯蒂的许多小说遵循一种公式化的结构，有效地营造出悬念。最初发现犯罪后，警察调查开始，采访所有嫌疑人。在整个过程中，克里斯蒂逐步释放线索，时而使不同的嫌疑人看似有罪，时而又将他们洗清。在读者认为自己已经解开谜团时，克里斯蒂会引入情节反转，比如不在场证明或新事实，颠覆读者的预期。人际关系的紧张和误导性的线索也帮助混淆了线索，直到最终的真相揭晓。 

Through her masterful character portraits, atmospheric settings, ingenious plotting, period research, masterful manipulation of expectations, and transparent prose, Agatha Christie revolutionized the Golden Age mystery genre. Even a century later, Christie’s novels continue to find new fans and influence modern crime fiction. Iconic detectives like Poirot and Miss Marple have penetrated global popular culture through countless television and film adaptations. It is through the original printed page that readers can still be gripped by her intriguing balance of misdirections and climax reversals and delight in her precise storytelling craft.

通过她精湛的人物描绘、富有氛围的背景、巧妙的情节构建、时代研究、对读者期待的巧妙操控以及清晰的文笔，阿加莎·克里斯蒂彻底改变了黄金时代的悬疑小说类型。即使在一个世纪后，克里斯蒂的小说仍然吸引着新的读者，并影响着现代犯罪小说。像波洛和马普尔小姐这样的经典侦探通过无数的电视剧和电影改编作品深入全球流行文化。正是通过原版印刷的书页，读者仍能被她引人入胜的误导与高潮反转所吸引，并欣赏她精确的叙事技巧。

Written By: Lesley Li

Title: "Story of Bananas 香蕉的故事"
Text:
"Story of Bananas 香蕉的故事
Image

Being one of the symbols of tropical culture, bananas, with their creamy texture and unique sweetness, are one of the most popular fruits on this planet. In summer, reading a book with a mouthful of bananas is always my favorite pastime. However, once when I read a book while peeling a banana, it all changed.

作为热带文化的象征之一，香蕉有着细腻的口感和独特的甜味，是地球上最受欢迎的水果之一。夏天，一边看书一边吃香蕉是我最喜欢的消遣方式。然而，有一次，当我一边剥香蕉一边看书时，一切都变了。

In One Hundred Years of Solitude, during a war, an utopian town called Macondo rained for four years, eleven months, and two days. Although it rains a lot in that hidden swamp, in real life it symbolizes something far more cruel—how a company used the sweetness of bananas to drown half of Central America into hell.

在《百年孤独》中，在一场战争中，一个名叫马孔多的乌托邦小镇下了四年十一个月零两天的雨。虽然那片隐秘的沼泽地经常下雨，但在现实生活中，它象征着更残酷的东西--一家公司如何利用香蕉的甜味将半个中美洲淹没在地狱之中。

Back in the late 1800s, the Costa Rican government decided to build a railroad in the country. Unfortunately, the country couldn’t afford the cost to finish this program in the rainforest, and it had proved to be really challenging to work in those conditions. Luckily, an American investor, Minor Cooper Keith, gave them a helping hand. In return, he asked for something more important than money—6% of the country’s land with a lease of 99 years. Also, the president of Costa Rica gave him tax reduction rights for this land. Unluckily, Keith was not satisfied at all. In providing labor and capital for building the railroad, Keith, this speculator, had amassed countless debts. How could he change all of this? Just on the other side of the Caribbean Sea, the answer was waiting for him.

早在 19 世纪末，哥斯达黎加政府就决定在国内修建一条铁路。不幸的是，该国无力承担在热带雨林中完成这一项目所需的费用，而且事实证明，在那样的条件下工作确实很有挑战性。幸运的是，一位美国投资者 Minor Cooper Keith 向他们伸出了援助之手。作为回报，他要了比钱更重要的东西--该国 6% 的土地，租期 99 年。此外，哥斯达黎加总统还赋予他对这块土地的减税权。不幸的是，基思根本不满意。在为修建铁路提供劳动力和资金的过程中，凯斯这个投机商积累了数不清的债务。他如何才能改变这一切呢？答案就在加勒比海的另一边等着他。

In 1870, a captain decided to have a rest in Jamaica because his ship had gotten damaged a few days ago. As a businessman, this captain called Lorenzo Dow Baker started looking for some special tropical commodities for extra chances to make money. Probably bananas are nice choices. He knew that bananas were popular among American consumers, but this fruit is a picky passenger that is hard to transfer—it goes bad easily in a couple of days because of its thin skin. Fortunately, this time the hand of destiny gave a push to him, and Baker found a unique kind of banana there—Big Mike. It was not very famous because of its thick skin. Without any hesitation, Baker brought tons of Big Mike to the North American market. Big Mike on the shelf led a yellow storm in that time. After Baker stroked gold from bananas, he found a problem: There were no more places for him to grow his bananas. That set up the perfect chance for Keith to meet Baker. They decided to collaborate together to start up an international business to sell tropical goods such as bananas in 1899.

1870 年，一位船长决定到牙买加休息一下，因为几天前他的船受损了。作为一名商人，这位名叫洛伦佐-道-贝克（Lorenzo Dow Baker）的船长开始寻找一些特殊的热带商品，以获得额外的赚钱机会。香蕉可能是不错的选择。他知道香蕉在美国消费者中很受欢迎，但这种水果很挑剔，很难转运，因为皮薄，几天就容易坏掉。幸运的是，这次命运之手推了他一把，贝克在那里发现了一种独特的香蕉--大麦克。因为皮厚，这种香蕉并不出名。贝克毫不犹豫地将成吨的 “大麦克 ”带到了北美市场。当时，货架上的 “大麦克 ”引领了一场黄色风暴。贝克从香蕉中淘金后，发现了一个问题：没有更多的地方供他种植香蕉了。这为基思遇到贝克提供了绝佳的机会。1899 年，他们决定合作创办一家国际公司，销售香蕉等热带商品。

This company is the United Fruit Company.

这家公司就是联合果品公司。

Keith turned more and more greedy since he started up this business. With his power in Costa Rica, Keith let his son-in-law and brother-in-law control the cabinet. His nephew even became the president of this country. Turns out, this private sector company had become a “state-owned business” of Keith’s family. This made it less necessary for it to improve its methods of production. Workers didn’t have much pay and had to bear nasty working conditions. Also, in order to ripen the bananas better, Keith asked workers to burn kerosene in plantations. This often caused explosions that killed innocent employees. Also, to prevent possible banana illnesses, all workers needed to coat toxic pesticides on their clothes and skin. Every day, countless workers lost their lives from this. Those who remained could only keep working in the poisonous banana forest day and night with exhaustion and the fear of death. This ignited a fire of revolution among workers.

凯斯自创业以来变得越来越贪婪。凭借在哥斯达黎加的权力，基思让女婿和妹夫控制了内阁。他的侄子甚至当上了这个国家的总统。结果，这家私营企业成了基思家族的 “国有企业”。这使得它没有必要改进生产方法。工人们没有多少工资，不得不忍受恶劣的工作环境。此外，为了让香蕉更好地成熟，凯斯还要求工人在种植园里燃烧煤油。这经常会引起爆炸，导致无辜员工丧生。此外，为了防止香蕉生病，所有工人都需要在衣服和皮肤上涂上有毒的杀虫剂。每天都有无数工人因此丧生。剩下的工人只能在有毒的香蕉林里日夜劳作，疲惫不堪，生不如死。这点燃了工人们的革命之火。

The next ruler of the UFCO was even more cruel. Samuel Zemurray, a genius at playing political tricks, expanded the “Republic of bananas” in Honduras. He assisted a previous president of this country, who hid in the United States, to create a new government with his own soldiers. This president gave him 10 thousand hectares of land and 25 years of tax-free rights as rewards for Samuel’s contribution. This provided chances for Samuel to better exploit the workers.

下一任 UFCO 统治者更加残酷。塞缪尔-泽穆雷是玩弄政治伎俩的天才，他在洪都拉斯扩大了 “香蕉共和国”。他协助躲藏在美国的该国前任总统用自己的士兵建立了一个新政府。这位总统给了他 1 万公顷的土地和 25 年的免税权，作为对塞缪尔贡献的回报。这为塞缪尔更好地剥削工人提供了机会。

Samuel did all of this to force the USA government to reduce the taxes on his bananas. After this, he realized one thing—if you can’t solve the problem from a government, you should solve the government itself. That was how Samuel “ruled” the banana industry in Central America: If workers dared to fight back, find their government to suppress them. If the government said no, suppress the old one and create a new one. This situation caused the tragedy of Colombian workers. In 1928, workers asked for better security on medication and health care during their work and rest for one day each week. Forced by the UFCO, the Colombian government police shot at workers in that strike, killing over 3000 innocent workers.

塞缪尔做这一切都是为了迫使美国政府减少对他的香蕉征税。在这之后，他明白了一个道理--如果你不能从政府那里解决问题，你就应该自己去解决政府的问题。塞缪尔就是这样 “统治 ”了中美洲的香蕉业：如果工人敢反抗，就找政府镇压。如果政府说不，那就镇压旧政府，建立新政府。这种情况造成了哥伦比亚工人的悲剧。1928 年，工人们要求加强工作期间的药品和医疗保障，每周休息一天。在哥伦比亚工人联合会的逼迫下，哥伦比亚政府警察向参加罢工的工人开枪，打死了 3000 多名无辜工人。

This is a black page of Colombian history—a scar that will never heal.

这是哥伦比亚历史上黑色的一页--一道永远无法愈合的伤疤。

In the yard of a small house sat a young boy beside his grandpa, who was listening to this story silently. His grandpa told him that the strike happened in a plantation called Macondo. The old man told the boy that Central America used to be a land with mighty rainforests and countless crops. But in order to kill the virus hidden in the soil, these banana sellers built reservoirs on this land. After that, nothing could grow on them except bananas. Every year and every day, non-stop. The boy wrote all of this in his book.

在一栋小房子的院子里，一个小男孩坐在爷爷身边，静静地听着爷爷讲这个故事。爷爷告诉他，罢工发生在一个叫马孔多的种植园里。老人告诉小男孩，中美洲曾经是一片拥有茂密雨林和无数农作物的土地。但为了杀死隐藏在土壤中的病毒，这些香蕉贩子在这片土地上修建了蓄水池。从那以后，除了香蕉，什么都长不出来了。年复一年，日复一日，从未间断。男孩把这一切都写进了他的书里。

The boy, Garcia Marquez, recorded the story of bananas in his pages. He recorded how officers in the bananas’ company shot at a boy just because he had hit them by accident. He recorded how the rain of Macondo washed everything away. He recorded how nobody believed that the bodies of dead workers filled a massive yellow train...

男孩加西亚-马尔克斯在他的书页中记录了香蕉的故事。他记录了香蕉连的军官如何因为一个男孩不小心撞到他们而向他开枪。他记录了马孔多的大雨如何冲走了一切。他记录了没有人相信，死去工人的尸体如何填满了一列巨大的黄色火车......

At the end of all of this, the solitude and the bitterness from Latin America grew into bananas, concealed by their soft and creamy taste. Could it really be covered?

在这一切的最后，来自拉丁美洲的孤独和苦涩长成了香蕉，被其柔软细腻的口感所掩盖。它真的能被掩盖吗？

Written By: Hestia Zheng

Edited and Translated By: Henry Chen

Title: "影评: 弗兰西斯哈(Frances Ha)"
Text:
"影评: 弗兰西斯哈(Frances Ha)


Frances, 怀揣着舞蹈梦奔跑跃动在黑白的纽约街道间，理想主义的火花在旋转中撒向她每一个如舞台一般的世界。她笨拙地生活在这个复杂的世界，好似有一层玻璃将她与这个世界所分开，将这个老成的孩子阻挡在成年人的世界之外。这种局外人的感受爆发在好友Sophie离开之后，这种离开绝不仅仅是距离的延伸，而更像是一种抛弃，或者说某种意义上的背叛——像是刚刚结束了一场原以为永远不会结束的梦。原本飘渺的现实转换成了不断增长的压力，推进着她与现实之间的磨合——不顾一切向前冲，跌倒，爬起，重新奔跑。现实使理想的火焰变得时隐时现，她始终用一种格格不入的真诚莽撞地冲进这个世界，直到遍体鳞伤才发现自己独自站立在黑暗中。

Frances, with the dream of dancing in mind, she runs and dances through the black and white streets of New York. The sparks of idealism are spinning and spreading into every stage-like world of hers. She lives in this complicated world, as if there is a layer of glass separating her from the world, blocking this mature child from the adult world. This feeling of being an outsider broke out after her friend Sophie left, this kind of departure was not just an extension of distance, but more like an abandonment, or a betrayal in a certain sense - like the end of a relationship that she thought had just ended. The originally ethereal reality turned into ever-increasing pressure, pushing her to adjust to reality - rushing forward regardless of everything, falling, getting up, and running again. Reality makes the flame of ideal appear and disappear. She always rushes into this world recklessly with an incompatible sincerity and realizes that she is alone once she is covered in bruises.

无数的片段零碎地记录着时间的流逝，也无声地记录下了她的选择。Frances 放弃了舞台上的聚光灯，而是选择转到了幕后，一切看上去都在往更好的方向发展，她完成了自己的妥协。Frances的生活就像一面镜子，让我们在其中发现自己的踪迹，瞥见未来的一隅——梦想能否经得起现实荆棘的考验，黑夜中熠熠生辉的理想主义火花如何撑过漫长的白天？

Countless fragments record the passage of time piecemeal and silently record her choices. Frances gave up the spotlight on stage and chose to move behind the scenes. Everything seemed to be moving in a better direction, and she completed her own promise. Frances’ life is like a mirror, allowing us to find traces of ourselves and glimpse a corner of the future - can dreams withstand the test of the thorns of reality, and how can the spark of idealism shining brightly in the night survive the long day?

Frances 一直对事物有独特的看法和追求，“我喜欢那些看起来像错误的事情。”（I like things that look like mistakes.），她期待一种极致的灵魂契合，她活在感受中，活在思考和探寻中。她的形象是一种个体普遍性的结合，是这个时代下群体性所面临的共同抉择。但她，这面镜子中，我们发现现实和理想并不总是对立的，理想的虚幻和美好是那么的难得，它必然会蒙蔽部分的真实，而现实却为那些阴翳带来了阳光，让我们真正清晰的看见自己到底想要什么，而所谓的妥协也只是披上了理想外衣的表象，而实质上是我们逐渐成熟的思考。

Frances has always had a unique view and pursuit of things, "I like things that look like mistakes."（I like things that look like mistakes.）, she looks forward to an ultimate resonance of soul, she lives in feelings, and in thinking and exploring. Her image is a combination of individual universality, representing the collective choices faced by many in this era. But in her, this mirror, we discover that reality and ideals are not always opposites. The illusion and beauty of ideals are so rare that they inevitably obscure part of the truth. Reality, however, brings light to those shadows, allowing us to clearly see what we truly want. What we call compromise is merely the appearance wrapped in the guise of ideals, while, it is the result of our gradually maturing reflections.

Frances ——Ha ！这个带有喜剧色彩的名字读起来也像是一种叹息，或是经历犹豫与抉择后与自己的最终和解。人生流逝于弹指间，在经历了所有世俗，纷争，压力，疲惫之后，也许一声“Ha”就足以概括很多——那最好的结束，也是重新的开始。

"Frances—Ha! This name, tinged with a sense of comedy, sounds like a sigh, or perhaps a reconciliation with oneself after moments of hesitation and decision. Life slips away in the blink of an eye, and after going through all the worldly struggles, conflicts, pressures, and exhaustion, maybe a simple 'Ha' is enough to sum up so much—the best kind of ending, and also a new beginning."

Written By: Cathy Zheng

Title: "How Different Philosophies Shape You 不同的哲学如何塑造你"
Text:
"How Different Philosophies Shape You 不同的哲学如何塑造你


Over the years, I’ve met many different people, each having different philosophies in life. What I find fascinating is how much these different philosophies shape the person who holds them.

多年来，我遇到了许多不同的人，他们每个人都有不同的人生哲学。我发现最吸引人的，是这些不同的哲学如何塑造持有它们的人。

One philosophy I’ve seen some have is what I like to call: “you-can’t-lose-when-you-don’t-try”. This is basically when you see people purposely not try so that when they fail, they can just blame it on the lack of effort and not have their skills questioned. When they succeed, they can even say they did it without even having to lift a finger. With this philosophy, it feels like one can only win and never lose. However, that is often times not the actual case. In fact, doing this can lead to falling behind peers, choosing to give up and “not try” in more and more things. While you may come to the conclusion that these people are just lazy, this may not be true. People with this kind of philosophy often have gone through hardships, and unlike all the superhero-y stories we’ve read, they weren’t able to overcome them. As a result, they choose to protect themselves with this philosophy. They choose to give up on themselves because in that moment, it was the least painful thing to do.

 我见过的一种哲学，我称之为“你不尝试就不会失败”。这基本上是指一些人故意不去尝试，这样当他们失败时，可以把责任归咎于缺乏努力，而不必质疑自己的能力。当他们成功时，甚至可以说自己根本没有费力气。持有这种哲学的人似乎总是能够获胜，而从未失败。然而，实际情况往往并非如此。实际上，这种做法可能导致他们在同龄人中落后，越来越多地选择放弃和“不尝试”。虽然你可能得出这些人只是懒惰的结论，但这未必是真的。持有这种哲学的人通常经历过艰难的境遇，与我们读到的所有超级英雄故事不同，他们没有能够克服这些困难。因此，他们选择用这种哲学来保护自己。他们选择放弃自己，因为在那个时刻，这是最不痛苦的选择。

At the other end of the spectrum is what I would call the “constant self-improvement” philosophy. This is when people try to improve every aspect of themselves and constantly strive for better. While you may think this is an amazing philosophy that leads to success, that is not entirely the case. I’ve personally tried this philosophy to a slight extreme and long story short, it was exhausting. Whenever something wrong happened in my life, I would always think of what I could have done better and what I could improve in. I would put the blame on myself even if it really wasn’t. Whenever someone does something better than me, I wouldn’t feel happy for them and instead feel frustrated at myself for falling behind. What’s even more frustrating is whenever I got worse at something. We always hear how accumulated constant self-improvement can lead to greatness, but often times forget that we should leave room for mistakes and “un-improvement”.

另一端是我所称的“持续自我提升”哲学。这是指人们努力改善自己各个方面，不断追求更好。虽然你可能认为这是导致成功的伟大哲学，但事实并非完全如此。我个人尝试过这种哲学，甚至有些极端，简而言之，这让我感到疲惫。每当我生活中发生不顺时，我总会想自己能做得更好，能改进什么。我会把责任归咎于自己，即使这并不是真的。每当有人比我做得更好时，我不会为他们感到高兴，反而会因为落后而感到沮丧。更令人沮丧的是每当我在某方面变得更差。我们常常听到持续自我提升的积累可以导致伟大，但常常忘记我们应该给错误和“不进步”留出空间。 

For most of the people I’ve met, they’ve settled for somewhere in between. Whenever they get motivated, they start trying hard for quick bursts. They strive hard in what they find important, but also know to let go whenever they need to. Whatever it is you choose to do, remember that no philosophy is guaranteed to lead to success. Along the way, adjustments would be needed based on the task ahead. Have an important exam coming up? Adjust for a more strive-hard mindset. Feeling exhausted? Take a few steps back allowing yourself to have the time and space to rest. Whenever the feeling strikes that what you’re doing isn’t quite right, take a moment to pause and think about how you think and what philosophy you have for your life.

在我遇到的大多数人中，他们选择了一个介于两者之间的地方。每当他们受到激励时，他们会短时间内努力尝试。他们在自己认为重要的事情上努力，但也知道在必要时放手。无论你选择做什么，请记住，没有任何哲学可以保证成功。在这个过程中，根据眼前的任务需要进行调整。即将面临重要考试？调整为更努力奋斗的心态。感到疲惫？退后几步，给自己时间和空间来休息。每当你觉得自己正在做的事情不太对时，停下来思考一下你的想法和你的人生哲学。

Written By: William Chen

Title: "对于高敏感所带来的问题，我们真的需要一个解决方案吗？"
Text:
"对于高敏感所带来的问题，我们真的需要一个解决方案吗？
Image

一个对于外界环境变化极其敏感的人，通常也对这个世界拥有极强的感知力。但“高敏感”这个特质却也会在这群人感受世界的同时，困扰着他们。

A person extremely sensitive to changes in their environment often has a heightened perception of the world. Yet, this trait of "high sensitivity" can also become a burden, making it hard for them to navigate life.

我便是一个鲜明的例子。陌生人在公共场合向我投来一个意义不明的眼神，便能使我胡思乱想一整天。抛开情绪方面的困扰不谈，周遭事物的变化对感官的刺激，也无时无刻影响着高敏感人群的生活。

I am one example myself. One vague look from a stranger in public can leave me overthinking about it for an entire day. Beyond emotional distress, the constant stimulation of senses affects every aspect of life for highly sensitive people.

对于这样的困扰，我们选择向外界寻求解决方案，可是好像从没有得到一个理想的结果。

To address these struggles, we turn to the outside world for solutions, yet never found the ideal answer.

似乎没有人在正面回应我们的诉求。因为我们只得到了两种答案，而当我静下心去思考这些答案，往往会发现它们很荒谬。它们真的是合适的解决办法吗？

It seems our concerns receive little direct response. We’re left with two kinds of advice, and when I think them through, they often seem absurd. Are they really the right solutions?

第一种就是去鼓励你做一个迟钝的，有钝感力的人，并且不要胡思乱想或不要在意其他人的看法。

One solution is to encourage us to become less sensitive, to stop overthinking or worrying about others’ opinions.

第一次听到这样的话，是在父母的口中。年幼的我不曾有过怀疑，因为我极度相信他们口中的那一句“爱哭又敏感的小孩做不成任何事”，所以我委屈地想要改变自己。但把这种转变真切地落实下去，似乎是我从小到大都无法做到的事情。而时至今日，我仍然可以听到这样的言论，无论是来自朋友，老师，长辈，还是其他人。

I first heard this from my parents. As a child, I didn’t question it—I deeply believed in their words that “a sensitive child who always cry could never accomplish anything,” so I tried to change myself. But truly carrying out such a change is a task I never succeed, even after years of effort. To this day, I still hear this advice from friends, teachers, elders, and all the other people.

于是我开始思考这个观点的合理性。假若高敏感人群真的想要通过“变得迟钝”来过得轻松的话，开始这一行动的难度会有多大？我的确尝试过，但是我失败了，并且失去了再一次这么做的勇气和精力。如果我需要掩盖自身的特点，转而成为“迟钝人群”的一员，我的存在是否就被全盘否定了？不同的思维或性格特质真的有高低贵贱之分吗？

Thus I started questioning its validity. If highly sensitive people want to “become unresponsive” to live more easily, how hard would it be to change? I’ve tried, but I failed and lost the courage and energy to try again. If I have to hide my nature and become “one of the insensitive,” doesn’t that deny my very existence? Are there really superior or inferior types of thinking or personality traits?

第二种答案，反其道而行之。他们会告诉你高敏感是一种天赋，因为敏感，所以你们在人际交往中善解人意，有很强的共情能力，因为敏感，所以你们还更擅长在生活与工作中发现错误、及时自我反思。

The second answer is the opposite approach. People tell you that high sensitivity is a gift. Because you’re sensitive, you’re empathetic in relationships, keenly aware of errors in life and work, and quick to self-reflect.

人们普遍认为这样的回答会让高敏感人群产生强烈的感动，从前的我亦是如此。但是从未消失的困扰促使着我一再思考，最终猛然发现这样被人夸口的品质都有着很强的利他性。这些所谓“美好且有益”的品质，无一例外地让我们更好地服务于整个社会，而非自己。

Most people suppose this answer to make sensitive people feel deeply touched, and I used to feel that way. But my persistent struggles led me to realize that these praised qualities have a strong altruistic nature. These “beautiful and beneficial” traits ultimately serve society, not ourselves.

可是无止境地利他却是造成内耗和焦虑的根源，所以这不是我们想要找寻的答案。这就好像我整日烟不离手，吞云吐雾，同时不断地为自己抽烟的陋习而感到羞愧与悲哀。我迫切地想要戒烟，却仍然被告知：“抽一根烟，让自己的生活变得更好吧。”

But endless altruism only breeds anxiety and inner conflict, which isn’t the answer we’re looking for. Imagine being chained to smoking, desperate to quit but constantly hear, “Have another cigarette, it’ll make your life better.”

我们永远被摆在社会发展的角度里，迎面而来的是从未终止的审判。他人没有看清高敏感的真相，却仍然盲目地给出偏离关键问题的答案。

Society always puts us on trial for its development. People don’t see the truth about high sensitivity, yet they keep giving solutions that miss the core issues.

于是我又开始天真地幻想起一个没有竞争与压迫的社会，想象着自己在这样的环境里生活该有多么轻松和快乐。但是幻想终究是虚假的，并且人们所说的那句“这个世界就是如此残酷”一直萦绕在我的耳畔，我终于发现，这一切似乎令我着急了——我急于找到一个解决方案，而忽视了所有高敏感曾带给我的，细腻而难忘的感受。我也忽视了一个事实：我将自我摆在了一个供人审视与批判的展台之上，可我忘记了我也曾因为这般审视与评价而流下眼泪。即使所有高敏感人士都生活在理想乌托邦，不讨喜的天气变化与突如其来的过度思考，都能够在一瞬间，再一次将我们击碎。

So, I naively dream of a society without competition or pressure, imagining how relaxed and happy I would feel. But at the end of the day, fantasy is fake, and the phrase “the world is just so cruel” always echoes in my ears. I’ve come to realize I was too eager for an answer, overlooking the delicate, unforgettable moments that sensitivity has given me. I also overlooked the fact that I had put myself on display for others’ judgment and critique, even though it only brings tears. Even if all sensitive people lived in an ideal utopia, an unpleasant change in the weather or a sudden flood of thoughts could still shatter us in an instant.

或许真正的答案只是简单的了解与包容。或许真正的问题并非敏感，而是错把敏感当成了真正的问题。因为敏感并非需要被修正的缺陷，也不是一种被天赋盖过弱点的品质。

Perhaps the true answer is simply understanding and accepting. Perhaps the issue is not sensitivity itself, but mistaking it as the problem. Sensitivity isn’t a flaw that needs fixing, nor is it a trait solely defined by its benefits.

因此，我们渴望更广泛的理解与包容，我们也渴望站在明处，坦然自在地，与所有人一起。

Therefore, we long for broader understanding and acceptance, and we also wish to stand in the open, comfortably, alongside everyone else.

Written By: Doris Jane

Edited and Translated By: Grace Cai

Title: "Question Everything 质疑一切"
Text:
"Question Everything 质疑一切
Image

We all have our (not religious) beliefs and understanding of how the world works. They are what guide our actions and where we go when we want to make sense of new situations. Usually, once accepted, a belief resides in your brain until it is forgotten or your brain rots, whichever happens first. However, the validity and usefulness of the belief usually do not last nearly as long. This is why we must examine our beliefs on a regular basis to see what value they still hold, if any.

我们每个人都有自己的（非宗教性的）信仰和对世界运行方式的理解。它们是我们行动的指南，也是我们想弄清新情况时的方向。通常，信念一旦被接受，就会留在你的大脑中，直到它被遗忘或你的大脑腐烂，以先发生者为准。然而，信念的有效性和实用性通常不会持续太久。这就是为什么我们必须定期审视自己的信念，看看它们是否还有价值。

Think of something that you believe, if you will. It can be anything from the belief that studying is more productive than playing to the belief in your own existence. Think about why you believe in it. Is it because you saw or experienced it? Is it because someone told you it was true and gave you convincing proof to believe it? Or maybe because it is just less troublesome to accept it as truth regardless of whether or not you actually believe it. Whatever reason you have, throw them aside first and pretend that they never existed.

Now question your belief.

请想一想你所相信的事情。可以是 “学习比玩耍更有效率 ”的信念，也可以是 “相信自己的存在 ”的信念。想想你为什么相信它。是因为你看到或经历过吗？是因为有人告诉你这是真的，并给了你令人信服的证据？又或者是因为无论你是否真的相信它，接受它为真理只是一件比较省事的事。不管你有什么理由，先把它们扔到一边，假装它们从未存在过。

现在，质疑你的信念。

Ask yourself: Is it true? Why is it true? What does it imply if it is true? Come up with reasons that you believe in and accept instead of consensus or “correct” reasons. For every answer you come up with, question it. Pretend that you are explaining to a toddler who does not understand anything. Don’t be content with basic explanations that intend to stop all thinking, especially ones along the lines of “because that’s just the way things work." Your goal here is not necessarily to arrive at an answer but to try to uncover the fundamental “truths” you hold that govern your life. As you dig deeper and deeper, check if there are inconsistencies in the reasons behind your beliefs. If there are, then either you are missing something, you do not a hundred percent believe in those reasons, or your beliefs are not firmly rooted in logic and reasoning.

问问你自己 这是真的吗？为什么是真的？如果是真的，它意味着什么？提出你相信并接受的理由，而不是共识或 “正确 ”的理由。对于你想到的每一个答案，都要提出质疑。假装你是在向一个什么都不懂的幼儿解释。不要满足于旨在停止所有思考的基本解释，尤其是那些 “因为事情就是这样 ”的解释。你的目标不一定是得到一个答案，而是试图发现你所持有的、支配你生活的基本 “真理”。当你越挖越深时，检查一下你的信念背后的原因是否前后矛盾。如果有，那么要么是你遗漏了什么，要么是你没有百分之百地相信这些理由，要么是你的信念没有牢固地扎根于逻辑和推理之中。

Do all beliefs have to be based on logic and reasoning? That is something you could question. Be careful of assuming things that are generally thought to be obviously true. Minimize that amount of beliefs that you have that are not backed up by reasons. It is sometimes unavoidable to believe in ideas with no deeper reason, but it's less common than you might think.

是否所有信念都必须基于逻辑和推理？这是你可以质疑的问题。小心假定那些被普遍认为是明显真实的事情。尽量减少没有理由支持的信念。相信没有深层原因的想法有时是不可避免的，但这种情况比你想象的要少。

What if you do not really know what you believe in? Another approach you could take is to look at certain actions you took and try to reason out your beliefs based on them. It is true, however (or is it?) that the reasons behind one’s action may have more to them than just one’s beliefs.

如果你真的不知道自己的信仰是什么呢？你可以采取的另一种方法是，看看你采取的某些行动，并试着根据这些行动推理出你的信仰。然而，一个人行动背后的原因可能不仅仅是他的信仰，这一点是真的（或者是真的吗？

You may eventually come up with a question to which you have no good response. Maybe you don’t know why you feel good after doing good to others. Maybe you don’t understand how different conditions could prompt you to do different things. When this happens, it might be time to do some research or ask for help from others.

你最终可能会提出一个你没有很好回答的问题。也许你不知道为什么与人为善会让你感觉良好。也许你不明白为什么不同的条件会促使你做不同的事情。出现这种情况时，也许是时候做一些研究或向他人寻求帮助了。

At the end of all this, you would have hopefully learned more about yourself, rejected outdated beliefs, and gained a better understanding for the things you choose to still believe in. Just because you found a new way to think about something, however, does not mean that it is the absolute best way to do it. Try attacking one problem from multiple angles; you may come up with different conclusions.

在这一切结束的时候，你有望对自己有更多的了解，摒弃过时的信念，并对你选择仍然相信的事物有更好的理解。然而，仅仅因为你找到了一种思考问题的新方法，并不意味着它就是绝对最好的方法。尝试从多个角度来解决一个问题，你可能会得出不同的结论。

Remember that updating your beliefs is a never-ending process. Our goal, therefore, is not to achieve a perfect understanding of the world but to constantly improve learning more about ourselves and the world around us.

请记住，更新你的信念是一个永无止境的过程。因此，我们的目标不是对世界有完美的理解，而是不断提高对自己和周围世界的认识。

Written By: Henry Chen

Edited and Translated By: Sarah Xu

Title: "Attention 注意力"
Text:
"Attention 注意力
Image

在Ulric Neisser, Robert Becklen and Daniel Cervone（人名）内的研究中，观众们正在观看两组人相互抛球的片段，而一名妇女则从他们中间走过。观看结束后，观众们能够详细指出游戏的过程。却没有注意到从他们身边走过的那位女士。为什么会这样？信息处理的缺失是如何导致许多事故发生的？

During the research of Ulric Neisser, Robert Becklen and Daniel Cervone, viewers were viewing a clip of two groups of people tossing balls across each other, while a woman walked through them. After viewing, the viewers were able to point out the process of the game in details. Not realizing the woman who passed by. Why so? How does the lack of information processing lead to many accidents?

回答这个问题的关键是了解注意力的概念。注意分为两类：无意识注意力和有意识注意力。我们有权选择关注哪些信息，有意识地感知这些信息。由于我们的信息处理能力有限，能被同时处理的信息只有几个。例如，在聚会中会有背景音乐。在与他人交谈时，你不会注意到其他外部信息，包括聚会中难闻的气味。这一过程被称为选择性注意，即在一段时间内专注于某一特定对象，同时忽略分心和无关信息的行为。此外，选择性注意的一种表现是，当我们的注意力转移到其他地方时，我们看不到可见的物体。这个过程就是 “无意盲”。

The key to answer the question is to know the concept of attention. Attention is divided into two categories: unconscious and conscious attention. We have the authority to choose which information to focus on, perceiving this information consciously. Due to the limited capacity of our information processing, not much of it can be thought for in one sitting. For example, there are background music in a party. When engaged in a conversation with others, you are not aware of other external information including unpleasant smells in the party. This process is known as selective attention, an act of focusing on a particular object for some time while simultaneously ignoring distractions and irrelevant information. Moreover, an occurrence of selective attention is that we fail to see visible objects when our attention is directed elsewhere. This process is inattentional blindness.

据美国国家安全委员会统计，大约有 160 万起车祸是由于驾驶员用手机发短信造成的。尽管许多人声称他们可以在驾驶时同时处理多项任务，但能够在不影响驾驶性能的情况下参与认知任务的人数比例估计约为 2%（Watson 和 Strayer，2010 年）。这是因为我们的注意力从道路和电子设备之间转移，还有认知任务要求我们有限的信息处理能力。

According to National Safety Council, roughly 1.6 millions of car crashes are due to drivers texting on mobile phones. Although many claim that they can multi-task while driving, the proportion of people who are able to participate in cognitive tasks without affecting their driving performance is estimated to be approximately 2% (Watson and Strayer, 2010). These are due to our attention shifting vis versa the road and our electronic devices, and the cognitive tasks demand our limited capacity for information processing.

总之，避免在某些情况下身兼多职对于预防许多事故至关重要。

All in all, avoiding multi-tasking in some circumstances is essential to prevent many accidents.

Title: "A Journey to Overcoming Study Anxiety 克服学习焦虑之旅"
Text:
"A Journey to Overcoming Study Anxiety 克服学习焦虑之旅
Original Ariana Chen Polarity CRS IHS校刊社
 Nov 26, 2024, 12:30 AM


As a transfer student, it has only been half a year since I transferred from a public school to my current school. At first, my life seemed seemed consumed by endless classes, exams, and project reports. The study pressure loomed over me like an invisible mountain, making it hard to breathe. However, after some exploration and practice, I discovered effective ways to manage and alleviate this stress.

作为一名转校生，从公立学校转到现在的学校才仅仅半年。起初，我的生活似乎被无尽的课程、考试和项目报告占据。学习压力像一座无形的山压得我喘不过气。然而，在一段时间的探索和实践后，我发现了一些有效的方法来缓解这种压力。

1. Learning Time Management 学习时间管理

I realized that pulling endless all-nighters and studying non-stop didn’t increase my efficiency. Instead, it left me exhausted and unproductive. By creating a detailed schedule, I started allocating time for study, rest, and leisure in a more balanced way. This approach not only made my studies more organized but also ensured I had time to relax and recharge.

我意识到，不停地熬夜和持续学习并不会提高效率，反而让我感到更加疲惫。通过制定详细的时间表，我合理地分配了学习、休息和娱乐的时间。这种方法不仅让我学习更加有条理，还确保了我有足够的时间放松和恢复精力。

2. The Power of Exercise 运动的力量

I found exercise to be a great stress reliever. Every afternoon, I would go for a run on the campus track or do strength training in the gym. Exercise helped my brain release endorphins, the “feel-good” chemicals, which boosted my mood. After exercising, I felt refreshed, and my study efficiency improved significantly.

我发现，运动是缓解压力的绝佳方式。每天下午，我都会去校园跑道上跑步，或者在健身房进行力量训练。运动可以帮助大脑释放内啡肽——一种让人感觉愉快的化学物质。运动后，我感到精神焕发，学习效率也大大提高。

3. Eating for Energy 运动的力量

A healthy diet became another crucial aspect of my stress relief strategy. I started paying attention to the nutritional value of my meals, cutting down on caffeine and sugar while incorporating more vegetables, fruits, and whole grains. These changes not only made me physically healthier but also kept my energy levels steady throughout the day.

健康的饮食也是我缓解压力的重要部分。我开始关注食物的营养价值，减少咖啡因和糖分的摄入，多吃蔬菜、水果和全谷物食品。这些健康食品不仅让我身体更健康，也让我保持充沛的精力。

4. Social Connection 社交联系

Social activities became an essential part of my routine. I regularly met with friends to share learning experiences and life updates. These interactions helped me relax and often provided new perspectives on solving problems. Sometimes, just sharing my stress with someone else was enough to make me feel lighter and more optimistic.

社交活动成了我日常生活中不可或缺的一部分。我会定期与朋友见面，分享学习经验和生活感悟。这些交流不仅让我放松，还为我提供了解决问题的新思路。有时候，仅仅是向他人倾诉压力，就能让我感觉轻松不少。

5. Relaxation Techniques 放松技巧

I also practiced relaxation techniques like deep breathing and meditation. Whenever I felt tense or anxious, I would find a quiet spot, close my eyes, and breathe deeply to relax my mind and body. These techniques helped me stay calm and find balance amidst the intensity of my studies.

我还学习了一些放松技巧，比如深呼吸和冥想。当我感到紧张或焦虑时，我会找一个安静的地方，闭上眼睛，深呼吸，让身体和心灵放松。这些技巧帮助我在高强度学习中找到平衡，并保持冷静。

6. Maintaining a Positive Attitude 保持积极的心态

Perhaps the most important lesson I learned was to maintain a positive attitude. I accepted that setbacks and difficulties are inevitable in the learning process. Instead of feeling defeated, I began to see challenges as opportunities to grow. Keeping a journal to record my progress and achievements boosted my confidence and motivation, reminding me of how far I had come.

或许最重要的一点是，我学会了保持积极的心态。我明白，在学习过程中，挫折和困难是不可避免的。但我相信，只要保持乐观，没有克服不了的挑战。我开始用日记记录自己的进步和成就，这让我更加自信和有动力去面对未来的挑战。

Through these methods, I not only reduced my study pressure but also improved my efficiency and well-being. Studying transformed from a burdensome task into an enjoyable pursuit. Each day became an opportunity to face new challenges with confidence, knowing I had the tools to handle them.

通过这些方法，我不仅减轻了学习压力，还提高了学习效率。学习不再是一种负担，而是一种乐趣。我开始期待每天的新挑战，因为我知道，无论遇到什么困难，我都能从容应对。

Title: "Thanksgiving: A Season of Gratitude"
Text:
"Thanksgiving: A Season of Gratitude


It’s been a long time since I last celebrated Thanksgiving. Even though it’s not something that people would always mark on their calendars, being thankful is something that everyone can do regardless of their country’s traditions. For me, this time of the year brings into focus the people and moments that make life meaningful.

我想我已经很久没有庆祝过感恩节了。这不是每个人日历上都会标记的日子，然而，感恩是一种无关国界和传统，人人都可以做到的事情。对我来说，这个时节让我更加关注那些让我生活变得有意义的人和瞬间。

Image

A tough moment I had a few days ago reminded me of this when I was so overwhelmed by stress from both inside and outside of school that I broke down and started crying. So I called my mom who is in the Philippines, and vented on about everything weighing me down for 30 minutes. She listened quietly, letting me get it all out. Then, without a second thought, she booked a flight back to China just to accompany me. 

几天前的一次经历让我深刻地感受到了这一点。当时，校内校外的压力让我不堪重负，以至于崩溃大哭。于是我拨通了在菲律宾的妈妈的电话，倾诉了整整30分钟，把心里的委屈和压力全都倒了出来。而她只是安静地听着，让我尽情发泄，然后毫不犹豫地订了飞往中国的机票，只为了来我身边陪我。

Image(picture of little Angela with her mom)

I am forever thankful for my parents, who have always been my greatest supporters. They let me be myself by supporting me in doing what makes me happy. My mom, especially, is so thoughtful and sensitive to how I’m feeling. Even the smallest change in my mood doesn’t escape her. When I was little, she was always the first person I’d run to when things got hard. Now that I’m older and living far from home, she’s still just as attentive, always making me feel cared for. She would always remind me to take breaks, go for a walk or catch a movie with friends instead of overworking myself. Apart from all this, she also encourages me to go for my dreams instead of living in other people’s expectations. Her words stay with me: “Even if you fail, it’s okay—every attempt is a step forward, a lesson learned.” Not just my mom, but my dad also encourages me by supporting my hobbies, even buying me concert tickets so I can see my favorite artists. Their unwavering support has given me the courage, the confidence to try, to stumble, and to grow.

我非常感激我的父母，他们一直是我最坚强的后盾，支持我追求自己的快乐，让我做真实的自己。尤其是我的妈妈，她总是那么细心，总能敏锐地察觉到我的情绪变化。小时候，每当我遇到困难，第一个想去找的人总是她；而现在，尽管我们相隔千里，她依然无微不至地关心我，总让我感到被爱和被在乎。她时常提醒我不要过度劳累，要停下来休息，散散步，或者和朋友看一场电影。除此之外，她还鼓励我追逐自己的梦想，而不是活在别人的期待中。她话始终激励着我：“即使失败了也没关系，每一次尝试都是向前的一步，是一次学习。”我的爸爸也是如此，他会为我的兴趣爱好提供支持，比如给我买我最喜欢的歌手的演唱会门票。是他们让我有了尝试、跌倒、再成长的勇气和信心。

ImageImageImage(picture of Angela with her friends)

When I think about Thanksgiving, I think of my friends, too. They’re like my second family, the people I would turn to when I need someone to talk to or just a little bit of comfort. Even the ones who are far away from me would always find ways to show they care about me—whether a random text to check in, a funny meme to make me laugh or a long video call to catch up. My friends can make even my worst days feel manageable. I honestly don’t know what I’d do without them.

说到感恩节，我也会想到我的朋友们。他们就像我的第二个家庭，是我需要倾诉或寻找安慰时会依靠的人。即使那些不在我身边的朋友，也总是通过各种方式让我感受到他们的关心。不管是一条随手的问候短信，一张让我捧腹大笑的搞笑表情包，还是一场漫长的视频通话，他们总能让我在即使最糟糕的日子里也感到温暖。我真的无法想象没有他们的生活会是什么样。

ImageImage（letters written by Angela's MYP teachers)

This Thanksgiving, I’m also thinking a lot about my teachers and how grateful I am for them. I often feel like they’re not just there to teach me knowledge in the textbook—they’re also the ones who help me through difficult moments, whether in class or outside of it. I’ve had teachers who have helped me with my studies after class just to help me catch up on something I didn’t understand, or who’ve offered me advice when I was stressed out about balancing everything I had to do.  They’ve shown me that learning isn’t just about grades but about growing as a person. 

在感恩节，我也特别想感谢我的老师们。他们不仅仅教给我课本上的知识，更是在我面对困难时给予支持的人。有老师在下班后花时间帮我补习，以帮助我赶上落下的内容；也有老师在我因学业和其他压力感到焦虑时给予我建议。他们让我明白，学习不仅是为了一个好成绩，更是为了成为一个更好的人。

Image(picture of the Korean guy who helped with luggages)

What’s more, I want to thank all the people who’ve helped me, even when I didn’t know them. I remember a time when my friend and I were struggling to carry our luggage up a slope, just the two of us. A kind Korean guy saw us and offered his help. He carried our bags to our destination, and by the time we got there, his back was covered in sweat. That small, unexpected act of kindness made all the difference, and I’ll always be grateful for it.

此外，我还想感谢那些曾经帮助过我的陌生人。有一次，我和朋友拖着行李箱爬坡，累得气喘吁吁。这时，是一个善良的韩国人主动提出帮忙，把我们的行李一路扛到目的地，而他到的时候已经满头大汗。这次意料之外的善意让我感激至今。

Image

This is a perfect time to reflect on how much there is to be thankful for--whether it’s the support of friends, the encouragement from teachers, the kindness of strangers or the love of my family. We often get caught up in the day-to-day struggles, but moments like these remind me that there’s so much to appreciate in the world, even in the smallest gestures. I’m grateful for the people who lift me up, those who help me when I’m down, and who show kindness without expecting anything in return. This holiday may be a time for reflection, but gratitude should be something we carry with us every day, in every moment.

这是一个完美的时机，去回顾那些值得感恩的点滴——无论是朋友的支持、老师的鼓励、陌生人的善意，还是家人无私的爱。我们常常被日常的琐事困扰，但正是这些小事提醒着我，世界上有那么多值得珍惜的美好，即便是最微小的善举也能带来温暖。我感激那些在我低落时拉我一把的人，感激那些无私给予关怀的人。感恩节是一个反思的节日，但感恩，更应该成为我们每天、每时都带着的心情。

Title: "Period "Herstory" － A Red Revolutionary"
Text:
"Period "Herstory" － A Red Revolutionary
Image

Once upon a time － yeah I know it sounds super cliché but that's how it goes － there was a grand and majestic castle, with two pink balconies, decorated by velvet curtains, by its side. Whenever the full moon rises for seven days, one or two princesses will appear silently on the balcony and go straight down to the central bedroom of the palace. There, servants would change all the silk blankets, clean the marble floor, and prepare a huge bed just for newlyweds － yes, princesses would stay here and wait for princes around the kingdom, who have to first go for a long running race and see if they could arrive at the castle － most of the time they couldn't. If our princess couldn’t find her lover in seven days, oops, she'll fall asleep forever. Servants will carry her and her bride price away. The followed cleaning job will last about another seven days, then it will start all over again the next month.

很久很久从前——好吧，我知道这听起来有点老套，但故事就是这么开始的——有一座宏伟壮观的城堡，在城堡的两旁，有两座装饰着丝绒窗帘的粉色阳台。每当满月升起的七天里，一或两位公主会悄无声息地出现在阳台上，然后径直走向城堡中央的卧室。在那里，仆人们会换上全新的丝绸床单，擦亮大理石地板，并为新人准备一张巨大的婚床——是的，公主会在这里等待来自王国各地的王子，而王子们必须先经历一场漫长的赛跑，以测试他们是否能抵达城堡——大多数时候，他们并不能成功抵达。而如果我们的公主在七天内找不到她的爱人，那么她将陷入永远的沉眠。随后，仆人们会把她和她的嫁妆抬走，接下来的清扫工作会持续七天左右，而这个循环将会在下个月再次开始。

I believe I have provided a vivid example of menses, menstruation, aka women’s period. The story shows the amazing process of how the egg from a woman's body came out of her nest and declined in her womb. In the next seven days, she will stay there for the sperm to visit her. That's how the period works － telling a girl that she is ready to raise a new life inside her body － the princess will become a queen. A powerful queen who could create the whole world under her dress.

我相信这个故事为大家提供了一个生动的类比——其实它所讲述的是月经，也就是所谓的“生理期”。那是一个神奇的过程：一个卵细胞离开女性的“巢穴”，进入她的子宫等待一粒精子的到来。这就是月经运作的原理——告诉一个女孩她已经准备好在身体里孕育新的生命——公主即将成为女王，而她将能够在裙摆下创造整个世界。

However, the price of this magic is costly. PMS and PMDD, these strange words that sound like computer brands are actually the nightmare for every woman who's stuck with the period. Because of the fluctuation of hormones, we might have these symptoms below －being anxious for no apparent reason, having poor concentration, or feeling angry and depressed at the same time. Physical symptoms include joint or muscle pains, headache, or trouble falling asleep. 

然而，这份“魔法”的代价却异常高昂。PMS和PMDD，这些听起来像电脑品牌的奇怪单词，实际上是每个被月经折磨的女性的噩梦。由于荷尔蒙的波动，我们常常会出现一些症状，比如莫名其妙的焦虑、无法集中的注意力，或是同时感到愤怒和沮丧。而生理上的症状则包括关节和肌肉的疼痛、头痛或失眠。

Image

Having read this truth about the menstruation, perhaps you gentlemen reading this can better understand some of the experiences of those around you, don’t you think? Girls often ask for sick leave during PE classes, although they seem as normal as other students. Your mother and sisters might act angrily in the morning, and then be blue in the afternoon for no reason. Those are all troubles they're facing while bleeding silently and feeling the pains they don't want to tell.

读到这里，我想各位读者中有些男士或许可以更好地理解身边的一些现象了吧？女孩子们经常在体育课上请假，即使她们看起来和其他同学也没什么不同。你的母亲或姐妹可能在某个早晨脾气暴躁，下午又莫名其妙地伤感。这些都是她们在默默流血和承受无法言说的痛苦时所经历的困扰。

Unfortunately, for “princes” and “kings”, most of them don't feel the same. According to the words of Greek Nature scientist Plinious in his book, menses is a form of curse which leads to drought and dying corps. In some Southern Asian countries such as Nepal and India, if girls are in period, their families will lock them in a narrow cabin in the wild for at least seven days alone. People in these regions also believed that menses is a disease only women have. They were regarded as evil spirits that bring bad luck, no one should touch them unless they want to kill themselves. In 2010, a 12-year-old girl died of serious diarrhea, because her parents refused to take her to the hospital for fear of the curse.

然而，遗憾的是，对于“王子”和“国王”们来说，他们大多无法感同身受。根据古希腊博物学家普林尼在他的书中所言，月经是一种诅咒，会导致干旱和作物死亡。在一些南亚国家，比如尼泊尔和印度，如果有女孩来了月经，她们的家人会把她们关进野外的一间狭小小屋里，至少七天。那里的人们还认为月经是一种只有女性才有的疾病，认为她们是不祥之人，谁碰她们就会倒霉甚至送命。2010年，一位12岁的女孩因严重腹泻去世，而她的父母因为害怕“诅咒”拒绝送她去医院。

When I read these records I could see women weeping through countless weeks of bleeding, tearing for the “magic” of new lives which turned to harmful curses － even though this was supposed to be a gift. I couldn’t help but wonder: Why can’t people around them take a moment to consider their actions? The "dirty" blood cleans the cradle for their newborns, and the "nasty" womb raises them. Those pairs of "filthy" breasts offer food for new lives.

看到这些时，我仿佛能看到无数女性为周复一周的痛苦而哭泣，为这“有害的诅咒”而流泪——而这本该是礼物，不是吗？我不禁想：为什么那些加害于她们的人就不能停下来多想想？那些“肮脏”的血为清理了新生儿成长的摇篮，那些“恶心”的子宫孕育了他们，那对“污秽”的乳房则为新生命提供了食物。

Image

Does stepping forward in history mean destroying everything from the environment which raised them? Without menses and other cycles inside women's bodies, none of the achievements of our civilization would exist.

历史的前进，难道意味着摧毁哺育他们的环境吗？没有月经和女性身体内的其他周期，我们的文明成就将无从谈起。

But even in the darkness of bias, women used their wisdom to fight against all the pressure in the past thousands of years. To hide better at first, they tried anything they could find to make lady pads － moss with mud, wild sponge, and even papyrus. Most of them lost their lives to infections of these dirty materials and bleeding too much. Later, wealthier ladies began using sheep wool or silk, while daughters of the poor used old clothes for pads. 

但即使在偏见的黑暗中，千百年来的女性也无时不刻运用着自己的智慧与压力斗争。为了更好地保护自己，她们尝试用任何能找到的材料制作卫生巾——裹着苔藓的泥土、野外找到的海绵，甚至是纸莎草。很多人甚至因为这些不洁材料感染或失血过多而丧命。后来一些，富家小姐开始用羊毛或丝绸，而贫民家的女儿则仍用旧衣服做卫生巾。

Fortunately, the world is developing fast. During World War I, some nurses who worked in the army found the perfect materials for convenient pads — cotton bandages. These anonymous great ladies wrote a letter to the American Fund for French Wounded. The organization sent the idea to the biggest paper company to produce modern pads for the first time in history.

幸运的是，文明的进步是飞速的。第一次世界大战期间，一些在军队工作的护士发现了制作方便卫生巾的完美材料——棉绷带。这些无名英雄向美国支援法国伤员基金会写信提议。该组织把这个想法送到了当时最大的造纸公司，于是最初的现代卫生巾问世了。

Image

In 1920, a black woman inventor named Marry Kenner designed sanitary belts to tie the pads better with underwear. Unfortunately, because of her gender and skin color, she didn't have the chance to apply the idea for a patent when she attempted in 1957.

1920年，一位名叫玛丽·肯纳的黑人女性发明家设计了卫生带，以将卫生巾更好地固定在内衣上。然而可惜的是，只因她的性别和肤色，她在1957年尝试申请专利时没能成功。

Now, let's go back to India. In 1998, when Arunachalam saw his wife using old rags for sanitary pads, he decided to make changes － make clean and cozy pads for the one he loved. He designed a machine to produce cheap pads with high quality. During the process of testing the pads, countless people laughed at him, even his wife tried to stop him, thinking that he had gone mad. But in the end, he made it, and his invention won the top prize in a competition for new techniques. People finally saw the need for Indian women because of his work. This saved generations of women in his country. For me, this was a touching story of revolution － the man's bravery and love became the sword to tear prejudice apart for Indian women, despite the patriarchal world he lives in trying again and again to strike him down. They failed to stop him, because this man stands for the will of countless women's will for equality － anyone who tried to stop the flood of rising should find themselves failed and hurt badly.

现在，也让我们把视线放回印度。1998年，当阿鲁纳恰拉姆看到妻子用旧布做卫生巾时，他下定决心，要为心爱的人制作既干净又舒适的卫生巾。他设计了一种机器，可以生产高质量且廉价的卫生巾。在测试这项发明的过程中，无数人嘲笑他，甚至他的妻子也认为他疯了而试图阻止他。但最终，他成功了，他的发明在一项技术创新比赛中获得了最高奖项。因为他的努力，人们终于意识到印度女性的需求。可想而知，这项发明拯救了多少女性！对我来说，这是一个感人而带有革命性质的故事——这个男人的勇气和爱，成为了撕裂偏见的利剑，尽管他生活在一个处处试图打压他的父权社会中。他们没能阻止他，因为这个男人代表了无数女性追求平等的意志——那些试图阻挡前进浪潮的人，最终只会发现自己被潮水冲刷的狼狈不堪。

Image

Here I implore you, especially to all gentlemen － respect the women around you: Your mother, your sisters, your friends. The world bestowed them with a power that both strengthened and weakened them. Women's strength is even more unbreakable than you think.

在这里，我恳请你们，尤其是男性读者——请尊重身边的女性：你的母亲，你的姐妹，你的朋友。这个世界赋予了她们一种既是力量也是负担的存在，女性的坚韧远超你的想象。

Anyway, I personally don't believe that this tiny little passage would make many differences, but I believe in the power of knowledge and civilization. Sometimes we just need some courage － courage to pass a small sanitary pad, courage to carry forward the spirit of red revolution with our hearts.

当然，我个人并不认为这小小的一篇文章能带来什么巨大的改变，但我相信知识和文明的力量。很多时候，我们需要的只是一点点勇气——递上一片小小的卫生巾的勇气，将这份“红色革命”的精神传递下去的勇气。

Title: "December 2024 Book and Movie/Film Recommendations"
Text:
"December 2024 Book and Movie/Film Recommendations
Image

Happy December to everyone! As we approach the close of the 2024 season, congratulations on all your hard work and achievements! To foster creativity and engagement, Polarity is excited to announce the launch of a monthly book/film review series, starting from December 2024 and posting on the first day of every month. This initiative aims to inspire thoughtful discussions and encourage everyone to explore new stories, ideas, and perspectives.

Book/s Recommendation

Siddhartha by Hermann Hesse

Image

A novel that follows the journey of a young man named Siddhartha in ancient India as he embarks on a quest for meaning and enlightenment. Raised as a Brahmin (member of the highest caste in the traditional Hindu caste system), Siddhartha feels dissatisfied with traditional teachings and decides to explore different paths, to find deeper meaning in life.

Through his journey, Siddhartha leans profound lessons about the nature of life, love and inner peace. The story explores on finding wisdom through personal experience, rather than following rules or teachings, and understanding how everything in life is connected.

Siddhartha is an inspiring read for anyone interested in spirituality, personal growth, or philosophy. It's a beautiful reminder that true fulfillment comes from within, not from external achievements.

Movie/s and Film/s Recommendation

Home Alone 

Image

This film tells the story of a young boy named Kevin, who finds himself home alone after his family accidentally leaves him behind during their holiday vacation. When two clumsy burglars target his house, Kevin uses his wit and creativity to outsmart them, embarking on a hilarious and heartwarming adventure. The film not only delivers plenty of laughs but also deeply explores the warmth of family and the power of love.

Kevin showcases remarkable intelligence and resourcefulness throughout the movie. He cleverly devises a series of traps and tricks that leave the two bumbling thieves utterly confounded, providing endless moments of laughter. His quick thinking and bravery not only keep viewers on the edge of their seats but also inspire pride in the young protagonist’s ingenuity.

Beyond its humor, the movie also portrays Kevin’s journey of growth with heartfelt nuance. He evolves from a boy who relies on his family into an independent and courageous individual, learning to face challenges head-on. His path is filled with obstacles but also brimming with warmth and poignant moments that resonate deeply.

In addition to Kevin, the film’s other characters are equally memorable and engaging. Kevin’s family, though absent for much of the story, conveys their love and concern for him in ways that form his strongest emotional anchor. Meanwhile, the two hapless burglars bring endless comedic relief, adding to the film’s lighthearted and entertaining tone.

Home Alone shines with its captivating storyline, endearing characters, clever humor, and heartfelt themes. It is a film that delights audiences of all ages while offering a meaningful reflection on the importance of family and the journey of growing up. More than just a comedy, it carries a timeless message, reminding viewers of the value of love, resilience, and personal growth—all delivered with warmth and laughter.

The Summer I Turned Pretty

Image

The Summer I Turned Pretty by Jenny Han is a book/movie full of youthful passion, happiness, and regret. It is a story about a girl, Belly, and her unforgettable summer memories at the beach house in Cousins Beach with Jeremiah and Conrad, boys who she had known since she was young and people who she characterized as friends, brothers, and crushes. As the relationships start to change in that one summer when Belly was 16 years old, the uncontrollable masked affection and flutter in the teenagers’ hearts gradually arise. Decisions that could lead to disappointment and growth must be made by Belly and the boys. It is an entertaining movie about the process of understanding yourself and the people around you and facing different situations.

Fantastic Mr. Fox

Image

Fantastic Mr. Fox is a stop-motion animation released in 2009, and the animation mainly tells the story of three farmers who fight against other animals in the underground. Different from the current general animal animation, the image of the animal is completely anthropomorphized, and this animation consciously retains the wildness of the animals themselves, which is also one of the important reasons why the story can develop.

At the beginning of the story, Mr. Fox appears as a free-spirited image, possessing the wildness that the author has given him, just like all wild animals. But then a family's responsibilities were overwhelmed by family and responsibility. In his ordinary life, Mr. Fox puts the responsibilities of the family above freedom. But as an animal, the wildness in his bones will not be easily consumed by the breeze of life, so when the opportunity comes, he chooses to pick up the "adventure" as a tool for animals to cope with challenges.

Adventures will eventually lead to trouble, but Mr. Fox will not sit idly by when he is given the image of a wild animal, and he unites other animals to face trouble head-on. His solidarity is like the survival instinct of animals, and it is like the release of the repressed nature of animals, after all, as animals, they still have the blood of struggle in their bodies.

As human beings, we are undoubtedly a villain in the story, and the animals are living their own protagonists' lives, and they have not stopped their steps because of any human behavior. In the end, Mr. Fox seems to have lost the free wildness he has been pursuing, but he has succeeded again and again with that wildness. Romain Rolland is very well-known as "There is only one heroism in the world: to see the world as it is, and to love it." Mr. Fox is looking for his own life and accepting his own life.
