Title: "保存在树脂冰淇凌里的甜蜜回忆"
Text:
"保存在树脂冰淇凌里的甜蜜回忆
Image

树脂作为一种多用途的材料，为艺术家们提供了一种将他们丰富的想象力具象化的方式。韩国艺术家Lurum巧妙地将小雕像封入半透明的棒棒糖中。她的作品系列《生活中的冰淇淋》捕捉了那些悬浮在甜蜜中的迷人时刻，并对记忆进行了既有趣又深思的探索。

Resin, a versatile material, gives artists a way to visualize and concretize their rich imaginations. Korean artist Lurum cleverly encapsulated small figures into translucent lollipops. In her work series, “Life in Ice cream”, she captured those mesmerizing moments that are suspended in sweetness and explored memories in a way that is both intriguing and thought-provoking.

Image

每件雕塑作品都由充满活力的光泽树脂渐变而成，看起来就像棍子上的可食用美食。Lurum甚至在每个棒棒糖上精心刻画了咬痕，赋予了作品更加逼真和诱人的外观。每件作品内含一个微型场景，透过其透明的形态，展现了童年时期的甜蜜回忆等主题。例如，一幅作品描绘了一位女士和一位男士一起跳舞的场景，而另一幅展现了两位骑自行车的人。

Each sculpture is made from a gradient of vibrant, glossy resin, looking like an edible treat on a stick. Lurum even carved bite marks on each lollipop, giving the piece a more realistic and alluring look. Each work contained a miniature scene, showing sweet memories of childhood and other themes through its transparent form. For example, a piece depicted a scene of a woman and a man dancing together while another work showed two cyclists.

ImageImage

Lurum的树脂雕塑虽然呈现甜蜜之感，却也蕴含着一种忧郁的氛围。艺术家在Instagram上阐述：“冰淇淋作为一种味觉上的享受，能够唤起甜蜜的快感，让人联想到安全与舒适。”“而另一方面，冰淇淋中的微缩模型则象征着生命中有限而脆弱的人类的记忆图像。” 通过《生活中的冰淇淋》系列，Lurum期望观众能够体验到双重形象——将生活中脆弱和不确定的记忆转化为像冰淇淋一样安全、甜蜜的存在。艺术家将这种转变称为“SWEETCH”（sweet与switch的合成词），它代表了一种理念，即将生活的记忆置于一个甜蜜、舒适的环境中，让它们被幸福地铭记。

Although Lurum’s resin sculptures evoked a sense of sweetness, but it also had a melancholic atmosphere. The artists on Instagram elaborated: “Ice-cream as a gustatory delight, evokes sweet pleasure, bringing feelings of safety and comfort.” “On the other hand, the miniature scene within the ice cream symbolizes the limited and fragile imagery of human memories in life.” Through the series of “Life in Ice cream”, Lurum hopes that the audience can experience a dual imagery—transforming the fragile and uncertain memories of life into a safe and sweet existence, just like an ice cream. Artist refers to this transformation as “SWEETCH” (a portmanteau of 'sweet' and 'switch'), it represents a concept of placing the memories of life in a sweet and comfortable environment, allowing them to be joyfully remembered.

Image

Lurum甚至创造了一个大型版本。

Lurum even created a larger version of the ice cream.

Image

树脂艺术家Lurum的系列作品《生活中的冰淇淋》捕捉了那些凝固在彩色半透明棒棒糖中的微型场景。每一件细节丰富的作品都提供了对记忆的有趣而舒适的探索。每件雕塑作品都由充满活力的光泽树脂渐变而成，看起来就像棍子上的可食用美食。

The resin artist Lurum's series “Life in Ice cream” captured miniature scenes encased in colorful, translucent lollipops. Each detailed piece offered an intriguing and comforting exploration of memories. Each sculpture is made from vibrant, glossy resin gradients that look like an edible treat on a stick.

Title: "Greene Kàrroll [连载]"
Text:
"Greene Kàrroll [连载]
ImageImage

The room smelled faintly of lavender, the plant which the Kàrroll family had sent as a present to Martha on her last birthday—and from the look of things it was really going to be her last. 

房间⾥弥漫着淡淡的薰⾐草⾹⽓，那盆薰⾐草是卡洛尔家族在玛莎上⼀个⽣⽇时送的礼物——这也许是她最后⼀个⽣⽇了。

Being terribly sick, Martha Knightley, head chef of the Kàrroll family, hadn't been taking care of the lavender plant for months, and its once vibrant purple blooms were now dulled to a bleak grey. The fragrance still lingered, barely detectable, but it was still there. The withering of Martha's plant had eventually attracted the attention of Martha's daughter, Lilac Knightly. But it was too late; weeks of tender nourishing couldn't prevent its fading beauty, however Lilac tried. 

卡洛尔家族的主厨玛莎·奈特莉因病重，已数月无力照料这株植物。昔⽇鲜艳的紫⾊花朵如今暗淡⽆光、憔悴枯萎，⾹⽓虽依旧萦绕，却⼏近⽆踪，唯余⼀丝淡淡的幽⾹。玛莎那日渐枯萎的薰⾐草引起了她⼥⼉莱拉·奈特莉的注意。然⽽已为时过晚，数周的精⼼呵护也未能挽回它逐渐凋零的美丽，任凭莱拉如何努⼒，终究是徒劳⽆功。

The fire in the hearth of Martha's bedroom crackled waveringly, the flickering light reflecting into Lilac's silver eyes as she sat on the mug by the fireplace, her arms wrapped tightly around her calves. She stared at the quivering flames emotionlessly, with a hollow look in her eyes. Her mother was getting weaker and weaker day by day, with no sign of recovering despite the help of the Kàrroll family. Thinking of chances that she might lose her mother soon, Lilac's eyes glistened with a sheen of unshed tears, the corners shimmering like dewdrops clinging to fragile petals. Her gaze remained fixed on the dancing flames, as if seeking solace in their chaotic beauty, but the firelight only deepened the melancholy in her eyes.

壁炉中的⽕焰在玛莎的卧室中摇曳不定，微弱的⽕光映照在莱拉银⾊的双眸中。她蜷坐在壁炉旁的地毯上，双臂紧紧环抱着小腿，面无表情地静静凝视着那颤动的⽕苗，眼神空洞而深邃。母亲的身体一日不如一日，尽管得到了卡洛尔家族的悉心照顾，依然毫无好转的迹象。想到她或将失去⺟亲，莱拉的眼眶中泛起泪光，眼⻆微微闪烁，宛若依附在脆弱花瓣上的晨露。她的视线依旧停留在跳动的⽕光上，仿佛试图从其混乱的美丽中寻求一丝慰藉。然⽽⽕光却愈发映衬出她眼中的哀愁。

"Come...here, my Lilac," Martha whispered. She lay in the dim light of the fireplace, her body a frail and feeble shell.

“过来……我的⼩莱拉……”玛莎低声呼唤，虚弱的身体宛如⼀具空壳。

"Yes, mother?" Staring at her mother's hollowed cheeks, Lilac couldn't help but feel distressed. She was trying her best to look at ease, because she knew that seeing her frown would only put Martha in greater torment. Martha tried to grip Lilac's hands, but she could only hold it faintly, her fingers slightly trembling.

“我在这⼉，妈妈。”莱拉微微前倾，凝视着母亲那深陷的面颊，心中不由得一阵酸楚。她尽力让自己表现得平静，因为她知道，⾃⼰表露出哪怕⼀丝的忧伤都只会让⺟亲更加痛苦。玛莎试图握住莱拉的⼿，却只能轻轻地拢住，指尖微微地颤抖着。

Image

"Look me in the eye," Martha said. "I have something to tell you, солнышко, listen carefully." 

“看着我……”玛莎虚弱地说道，“我有件事要告诉你，亲爱的，听好了。”

Leaning slightly forward, Lilac gazed at her mother firmly and intently.

莱拉微微前倾，坚定⽽专注地望着母亲。

"Stay away from Miss Greene Kàrroll," her mother said. “She's a witch!" 

“远离格琳·卡洛尔⼩姐......”玛莎低声说道，“她是个女巫！”

Her voice faltered on the last word, fragile and trembling, hanging in the air like a fading note. Her chest rose one last time before falling into a complete stillness. The room, once echoing with her voice, held a deadly and uncanny silence. Her mother's stiff, cold hands fell from hers.

她的声⾳在说最后⼀个字时颤抖着，脆弱而模糊，仿佛一声即将消散的余音飘绕在空气中。玛莎的胸⼝最后⼀次微微起伏，随即归于彻底的平静。曾回荡着她声⾳的房间，瞬间陷⼊了死寂⼀般的沉默。玛莎冰冷僵硬的⼿从莱拉的掌⼼滑落。

Lilac stood, stunned, her lips quivering, her eyes widening. Her mind churned with dread, staring at her mother’s breathless body. Was this really to be her life? A future with bruises and fear? Days and nights punctuated by her father's fierce rage? She could see it clearly now, all the violence—the slaps, the choking grips, the endless threats.

莱拉呆呆地站着，双唇微颤，双眼逐渐睁大，内心被一种深深的恐惧攫住，目光凝视着母亲那停止了呼吸的身体。难道这真是她的未来吗？——⼀个⽇⽇夜夜被⽗亲的暴怒⽀配的、充满淤⻘与恐惧的未来。她仿佛已预⻅了那些可怕的场景——那⼀记记⽿光、窒息般的勒痕以及⽆穷⽆尽的威胁。

But a spark of defiance flickered within her. A new question arose: Could she escape this fate?

然而，心底微弱的反抗之火悄然燃起，一个新的念头浮现于脑海：她能否逃离这命运的束缚？

Title: "I Love It When It Rains"
Text:
"I Love It When It Rains
Image

    People don’t like it when it rains. Some even hate it, preferring bright, sunny, normal weather over dark, gloomy, unpredictable weather. From a single drop to light drizzles, then heavy thunderstorms; it doesn’t sound like it gets any better. People are put into situations: running late, getting soaked, catching colds, unable to go home, jamming roads, causing accidents, flooding—adding noise and work to our daily lives.

    人们不喜欢下雨天。有些人甚至讨厌下雨，他们更喜欢明亮、晴朗、正常的天气，而不是阴暗、潮湿、难以预测的天气。从一滴小雨到淅淅沥沥的小雨，再到雷雨交加；听起来似乎并没有变得更好。人们陷入这样的境地：迟到、淋雨、感冒、无法回家、堵塞道路、引发事故、洪水—给我们的日常生活增添了噪音和工作。

    Seeing the rain makes us think our day is ruined.

    看到下雨，我们会觉得一天都毁了。

    Watching it makes us believe we’re so unfortunate.

    看着雨会让我们相信自己是如此不幸。

    “Why here?”

    “为什么在这里？”

    “Why at this moment?”

    “为何此时此刻？”

    “Unpredictable. It’s so unpredictable.”

    “无法预料 真是难以预料”

But why is the rain always a bad thing? 但为什么雨总是坏事呢？

    “Rain, rain, go away. Come again another day.”

    “雨，雨，走开。改天再来”

    When it rains, we think of things that should be kept inside. We open our umbrellas and close our minds. We try to keep ourselves dry as much as possible, focusing on staying on that spot under cover. It’s as if the rain is something to escape from, something that only gets in the way. We avoid the rain too much, treating it as nature’s curse, like a rose’s thorns. Why don’t we welcome it like any other weather?

    下雨的时候，我们会想起那些应该留在屋子里的东西。我们打开雨伞，闭上双眼，我们尽量让自己保持干爽，集中精力待在有遮挡的地方。仿佛雨是一种可以逃避的东西，是一种只会碍事的东西。我们过于躲避雨水，把它当作大自然的诅咒，就像玫瑰的刺一样。为什么我们不能像迎接其他天气一样迎接雨呢？

    Every moment I find it raining outside, I get this instant feeling of running outside to leave myself with the rain. Its presence brings the feeling of beauty in gloom and happiness in loneliness.

    每当我发现外面下雨的时候，我都会有一种瞬间的感觉，想跑到外面去，让自己与雨为伴。雨的存在让人在阴郁中感受到美丽，在孤独中感受到幸福。每当我发现外面下雨的时候，我都会有一种瞬间的感觉，那就是跑到外面，让自己与雨为伴。雨的存在给我带来了阴郁中的美丽和孤独中的幸福。

    But I don’t. I don’t walk or run through the rain—because no one else seems to feel that way. No matter how much I want to soak myself in its gentle and comforting presence, I’m just like everyone else. I’m afraid of getting wet, catching a cold, and possibly looking pitiful or foolish. I’m easily moved by what others think. Still, whenever I hear people complain about the rain, I stay calm and hold onto my quiet appreciation for it. I listen closely to the pitter-patter and reach for the drops outside the window. Because I know how much it means to me, even if it isn’t to others.

    但我没有。我不会在雨中漫步或奔跑，因为似乎没有人有这种感觉。无论我多么想让自己沉浸在雨的温柔和舒适中，但我和其他人一样。我害怕淋雨，害怕感冒，害怕看起来可怜或愚蠢。我很容易被别人的想法打动。尽管如此，每当听到人们抱怨下雨时，我都会保持冷静，静静地欣赏雨景。我仔细聆听着淅淅沥沥的雨声，伸手去接窗外的雨滴。因为我知道它对我来说有多重要，即使它对别人来说并不重要。

    We can never control the weather, nor even predict it so well. 我们永远无法控制天气，甚至无法很好地预测天气。

    We don’t know exactly when it will start raining or if there will be any thunderstorms. Whether we’re inside or outside, with or without an umbrella, it could still rain any time. And we can’t always be prepared for it. But we could accept it—the surprise. 

    我们不知道什么时候会开始下雨，也不知道是否会有雷雨。无论我们是在室内还是室外，有伞还是没伞，随时都有可能下雨。我们不可能总是做好准备。但我们可以接受它—惊喜。

    The weather is a reminder that life is full of surprises, both good and bad. Our job is to accept and appreciate the weather, whatever it may be. Because when you’re grateful for everything, it all turns into happiness.

    天气提醒我们，生活中充满了惊喜，有好有坏。我们的工作就是接受和欣赏天气，无论它是什么样子。因为当你对一切心存感激时，一切都会变成幸福。

    I’ve learned to be grateful for whatever weather comes my way. I’m thankful for the sun’s warmth and light and all its contributions to nature yesterday.  I’m thankful for the rain’s silent farewell today. I’m even thankful for the thunderstorms that shake the sky, pouring us its wrath and terror, reminding me of my childhood. I’m thankful for the rainbows that prove beauty lingers after a storm. And I’m grateful for the boy standing beside me, umbrella in hand, as we enjoy our simple moment together in the streets.

    我学会了对任何天气都心存感激。昨天，我感谢太阳的温暖和光芒，以及它对大自然的所有贡献。 我感谢今天雨水的无声告别。我甚至感谢震撼天空的雷雨，它向我们倾泻着愤怒和恐惧，让我想起了童年。我感谢彩虹，它证明美丽在暴风雨后依然存在。我感谢站在我身旁的男孩，他手持雨伞，我们一起在街头享受这简单的时刻。

    We’re reminded but don’t pay attention. Every day has a weather: giving us bright and gloomy days.

    我们被提醒，却没有注意。每一天都有天气：给我们晴朗和阴沉的日子。

The rain stops. 雨停了。

    We may forget in the moment, that we can’t have rainy days forever. Maybe it would rain for the entire day, a few days, or even a whole week. But still, the rain stops. 

    此刻我们可能会忘记，我们不可能永远拥有雨天。也许雨会下一整天，下几天，甚至下一个星期。但雨还是停了。

    Just like when cars idle as they are stuck in traffic, children patient for their parents’ umbrellas, and stray dogs hiding in stores on the street, we endure the waiting in those moments, knowing things will still go our way. Rain is like the beginning and end of chapters. We’ll never know when it starts or ends, having good and bad endings to surprise us and keep us going.

    就像堵在路上的汽车空转，孩子们耐心地为父母撑伞，流浪狗躲在街上的商店里，我们在这些时刻忍受着等待，因为我们知道事情还是会按照我们的意愿发展。雨就像章节的开始和结束。我们永远不知道它何时开始，何时结束，有好的结局，也有坏的结局，让我们惊喜，让我们继续。就像堵在路上的汽车空转，孩子们耐心地为父母撑伞，流浪狗躲在街上的商店里，在这些时刻，我们忍受着等待，因为我们知道一切都会按照我们的意愿进行。雨就像章节的开始和结束。我们永远不知道它何时开始，何时结束，有好的结局，也有坏的结局，让我们惊喜，让我们继续。

We miss those rainy days. 我们怀念那些雨天。

    And sometimes we even miss those days. We long for the warmth of summer in winter and the playful snow of winter in summer. Sometimes we are too busy to recognize and acknowledge our present weather. Sometimes, instead of wishing for rain on a hot summer day, why not just watch over the sun and appreciate the weather today?

    有时我们甚至会怀念那些日子。我们渴望冬天里夏天的温暖，夏天里冬天的嬉雪。有时候，我们太忙了，以至于无法认识和承认我们现在的天气。有时，与其在炎热的夏天盼望下雨，为什么不守望太阳，欣赏今天的天气呢？

    Because that day will come, we just don’t know when.

    因为那一天终会到来，只是我们不知道是什么时候。

Selected phrase: I listen closely to the pitter-patter and reach for the drops outside the window. Because I know how much it means to me, even if it isn’t to others.

选句：我仔细聆听着窗外的滴答声，伸手去接那滴答声。因为我知道这对我意味着什么，即使对别人来说不是。

Title: ""it don't matter if you’re black or white""
Text:
""it don't matter if you’re black or white"
Image

我应该在此处放上迈克尔·杰克逊的《Black or White》来为此篇文章开头。此歌的黑与白能让人联想到他的外貌变化，一个既令他痛苦又令别人感到怪异的转变，而这重塑了我对种族与肤色概念的理解。

I should begin this article with Michael Jackson's Black or White. The song's theme of black and white evokes thoughts of his physical transformation—a change that caused him both pain and drew curiosity from others. This transformation reshaped my understanding of race and the concept of skin color.

网络上曾有迈克尔杰克逊漂白皮肤的传闻，有人说他厌恶并背叛了自身的黑人身份，所以他整容，以迎合白人群体的审美。他因为白癜风而变浅的肤色也饱受争议。

There were rumors online that Michael Jackson had bleached his skin, with some claiming that he despised and betrayed his Black identity, undergoing plastic surgery to conform to the aesthetic standards of White society. His lightened skin tone, caused by vitiligo, also sparked considerable controversy.

种族，不仅包含肤色，还有文化。那些有着爆炸头的黑人们，被无数次告知，他们的命运是成为穷人、毒贩，甚至可能是囚犯。而迈克尔的突然出现，让如此多的黑人开始拥有一种梦想的勇气，因为他们发现和他们外表一致的黑人也有能力站在如此高的位置。

Race encompasses more than just skin color—it also includes culture. Black individuals with afros have often been told repeatedly that their fate is to remain poor, to become drug dealers, or even prisoners. Michael's sudden rise to prominence inspired countless Black people to dare to dream, as they saw someone who looked like them reach such great heights.

Image

但几年后，迈克尔的外貌变得越来越不像“黑人”，他似乎迫不及待地想要融入新的社群，于是他留着拉直的头发，在镜头里露出雪白的皮肤和瘦削的鼻梁。曾把迈克尔视为偶像的黑人们感到了失落，因为迈克尔曾让黑人们相信自己能够走得更远，可他最终把同胞们抛在身后。这群黑人不知道自己也被困在刻板印象中，尽管这不是他们的错。

But a few years later, Michael's appearance began to look less and less "Black." He seemed eager to integrate into a new community, sporting straightened hair, pale skin, and a slender nose in front of the camera. Black individuals who once idolized him felt a sense of loss. Michael had inspired them to believe they could go further, but in the end, he appeared to leave his own people behind. What they didn't realize was that they, too, were trapped by stereotypes—though this was not their fault.

黑人种族对于自身文化被遗弃的伤感和憎恨在此刻变得清晰。所以他真的忘记自己是谁了吗？或者，他真的遗弃了黑人文化吗？并没有，因为他拒绝用一生去做一个有色人种。

The sadness and resentment within the Black community over the perceived abandonment of their culture became especially evident at this moment. So, did he truly forget who he was? Or did he really abandon Black culture? The answer is no—because he refused to spend his life defined solely by being a person of color.

Image

他不染金发，也不带蓝色美瞳，他还会在巡演的时候把自己年幼的照片放在大屏上，观众和他都能清楚地看见那个拥有爆炸头与黑棕色肌肤的男孩。他的舞蹈总是有非洲舞的影子，他也热爱穿军装夹克，这曾是黑奴用主人丢掉的旧军装等服饰在节庆日表达个性的方式，里里外外都写满了“我拒绝被我的种族身份所限制”。

He didn’t dye his hair blond or wear blue contact lenses. During his tours, he often displayed childhood photos of himself on large screens, where both the audience and he could clearly see the boy with an afro and dark brown skin. His dances always carried traces of African movements, and he loved wearing military-style jackets—a nod to how Black slaves once repurposed their owners’ discarded military uniforms to express individuality during celebrations. Every aspect of him proclaimed, “I refuse to be confined by my racial identity.”

他从未体现出任何对黑人男性的刻板印象，譬如罪犯，他也始终没有被负面的标签所束缚，这是他对成为任何人的n*gger的抵制。他在黑人文化中获得了史无前例的自由。

He never embodied any of the stereotypes associated with Black men, such as being labeled a criminal, nor was he ever confined by negative labels. This was his resistance to becoming anyone's "n*gger." He achieved an unprecedented level of freedom within Black culture.

Image

他不断向世界证明，黑人不只是我们认为的那样。如果我们只能接受他的容貌固定在刻板印象范围之内并加以评价和攻击，这就是另一种歧视。

Michael continually demonstrated to the world that being Black was not limited to the narrow definitions people imposed. If we can only accept his appearance when it conforms to stereotypical expectations—and judge or attack him otherwise—then that, too, is a form of discrimination.

迈克尔为世界黑人做了无法衡量的好事，他的一生如此炳耀，他不该被如此对待。我并不想重提他的苦难，但我们都应该记住他黑棕色的肌肤下，仍在茁壮生长的是什么。

Michael did immeasurable good for Black people around the world. His life shone so brightly that he should never have been treated this way. I do not wish to dwell on his suffering, but we must all remember what continued to thrive beneath his dark brown skin.

Image

我将以写在《Black or White》MV里的一句话结尾，这是一句长响且振聋发聩的呼号：

I will end with a line from the Black or White music video—a resonant and deafening call to action:

Prejudice is ignorance.

Title: "Envy 羡慕"
Text:
"Envy 羡慕
Image

In Chinese, we have an old saying called “One takes on the color of one’s company. Well, every line exists for a reason, in real life most of us would be super glad to have some top dogs as our close friends. Unfortunately, when they share their happiness with us for holding the gold medal of a competition or a math exam paper with full marks, the first thing we taste in our mind might not be the same joyousness.

中国有句古话叫“近朱者赤”。世间万物皆有因，在现实生活中，我们大多数人都非常乐意与一些佼佼者成为挚友。但不幸的是，当他们与我们分享赢得比赛金牌或是数学考试满分的喜悦时，我们内心首先涌起的可能并非同样的快乐。

Have you ever caught a very strange feeling when looking at your company who is better than you, just like worms wriggling weirdly inside your stomach, making you sick and really want to puke?

你可曾在面对比自己优秀的同伴时，有一种极为怪异的感觉，就像有虫子在胃里奇怪地蠕动，让你恶心，甚至想要呕吐？

Have you ever asked yourself some really sharp questions?

- Why I‘m not the person who is glowing on the podium, even though I also worked as hard as he or she did?

- Why the happiness from the winner, who is my friend, is hurting me?

- Why am I hating the person who is so outstanding and cares about me? 

你可曾问过自己一些尖锐的问题：

- 为何站在领奖台上光彩照人的不是我，尽管我和他/她一样努力？

- 为何朋友作为胜利者的喜悦会刺痛我？

- 为何我会讨厌那个如此杰出且关心我的人？

Image

Unluckily, no one could give the exact answers to these question marks. Till now many of us are still struggling with these questions with the feeling, and her twin sister, jealousy. Many things happened because of these two naughty siblings.

不幸的是，没人能确切回答这些问题。直至如今，我们许多人仍在被这些问题以及它的孪生姐妹——嫉妒所困扰。诸多事情因这两个“调皮鬼”而起。

Being a huge fan of the musical play Alexander Hamilton, I was deeply attracted by the resilience passion, and talent of the American founding father himself: Living in a time when countless geniuses shone, his fame still burnt like wildfire in the late 18th century. However, every audience who ever witnessed the story knows that Alexander’s fate was tied to another figure, another gifted man who had the same intelligence-- Aaron Burr. For Burr, all he had experienced was extremely unfair from his perspective, compared to Mr.Hero. These two people were like the head and the tail of the same penny: They lost their parents as young boys, joined the war to fight for their country, and even worked and wrote in the same cabinet. But they were so different from the start. One “has nothing to lose”, with no titles or wealth at the beginning, who never throws away his shot. One “has something to prove”, being forced to carry the legacy and pride of his family name, always waiting for the chance and watching which wind will blow.

我是音乐剧《亚历山大·汉密尔顿》的忠实粉丝，深深被这位美国开国元勋的坚韧、热情与才华所吸引。他生活在一个天才辈出的时代，即便如此，他的声名在 18 世纪后期仍如野火般蔓延。然而，每一位看过这个故事的观众都知道，亚历山大的命运与另一个人物紧密相连，那是另一个同样天赋异禀的人——亚伦·伯尔。在伯尔看来，与这位英雄相比，他所经历的一切都极不公平。这两人就像同一枚硬币的正反两面：他们幼年都失去了父母，都投身战争为国而战，甚至在同一内阁共事、写作。但他们从一开始就截然不同。一个“一无所有”，起初没有头衔与财富，从不放过任何机会；一个“需要证明自己”，背负着家族姓氏的遗产与骄傲，总是等待时机，见风使舵。

In the whole play, the feeling of envy always stays alive inside Burr. Even though he is the “narrator” of the story on the stage, as audiences we can still see through his real thoughts between his lines. His theme song “Wait for It” is the showstopper among all the tunes, from it we could see his hesitation, vacillation, and ambivalence inside his chest. He was not as lucky as Hamilton till the end: George Washington chose Alexander as his secretary, not Burr. Alexander fought with glory in the last combat, when Burr was sick because of sunstroke. Alexander chose others to be the president, causing Burr to give up his shot. Deep inside, he must watched Alexander’s back enviously, this person had all the things he wanted: the support from friends and partners, the appreciation of the general, the love from his wife. However, after years and years, this kind of enviousness turned into jealousy and hatred with bitterness, forcing him to fire the deadly shot in that famous duel.

在整部剧中，嫉妒之情始终在伯尔心中萦绕。尽管他在舞台上是故事的“叙述者”，但作为观众，我们仍能从他的台词间洞悉他的真实想法。他的主题曲《等等看》是所有曲目中最精彩的部分，从中我们能看到他内心的犹豫、彷徨与矛盾。他始终不如汉密尔顿幸运：乔治·华盛顿选择亚历山大做秘书，而非伯尔。亚历山大在最后一场战斗中荣耀奋战时，伯尔却因中暑而抱恙。亚历山大选择他人成为总统，致使伯尔放弃了自己的机会。在内心深处，他必定嫉妒地望着亚历山大的背影，这个人拥有他所渴望的一切：朋友与伙伴的支持、将军的赏识、妻子的爱。然而，年复一年，这种嫉妒演变成了充满苦涩的怨恨与仇恨，迫使他在那场著名的决斗中射出了致命一枪。

For this occasion, I dislike this pathetic vice president at first, but once of a sudden, I realized that maybe I am another Burr in my story, who just hasn’t pulled the “trigger” right now.

起初，我很讨厌这位可怜的副总统，但突然之间，我意识到，或许在我的故事里，我就是另一个伯尔，只是还尚未扣动“扳机”。

Image

When I was younger, I used to have an excellent friend like that. She was so perfect: the girl never showed any negative thoughts or actions to anybody, always being friendly; She worked extremely hard with her own talents in math and a wide range of subjects, always taking the lead in our class; also she always wore a sweet and soft smile on her face, with her gentle manner. In one word everyone loves her. I, a student filled with hesitation and fear of my campus life, admired and appreciated her deeply.

在我年少时，曾有过一位那样出色的朋友。她近乎完美：从不对任何人表现出负面的想法或行为，总是友善待人；她凭借自身在数学及众多学科的天赋努力学习，在班级中总是名列前茅；而且她脸上总是带着甜美温柔的笑容，举止优雅。总之，每个人都喜爱她。而我，一个对校园生活充满犹豫与恐惧的学生，深深地钦佩并欣赏她。

But it seems that her existence broke the balance of my heart. In our math class, I was the only girl and often got left behind by others, for this reason, my previous teacher set a lower barrier for me to cross frequently while other students needed to reach their limit every time. Definitely, the rule disappeared when she came along--raising her hand high for every math problem, offering her homework with A*and 100 marks every day, and reaching the highest score in every exam and test.....

但她的存在似乎打破了我内心的平衡。在数学课上，我是唯一的女生，常常落后于其他人，因此，我之前的老师常常为我降低达标要求，而其他同学每次都需竭尽全力。而当她出现后，这一规则自然消失了——她每道数学题都高高举手，每天都交上 A*和满分的作业，每次考试测验都取得最高分……

Till then I was only envious of that because she deserves all of this. Unluckily, once when I decided to collaborate with her in a contest, she delayed me out of our team without any notice by accident, which meant I lost the qualification for joining it in that year.

在那之前，我只是羡慕她，因为她当之无愧。但不幸的是，有一次我决定和她组队参加一场竞赛，她却意外地在未告知我的情况下将我排除在团队之外，这意味着我当年失去了参赛资格。

Image

A few days before the contest when I was talking about the coming events I really loved with high expectations with my teacher, she frowned and told me that the girl already found another teammate and stopped working with me. Those days were already dark enough for me: the pressure from important exams and student council, having trouble having new friends, thus this bad news just rubbed salt in the wound.

竞赛前几天，当我满怀期待地和老师谈论即将到来的赛事时，老师皱着眉告诉我，她已经找了另一位队友，不再与我合作。那段日子对我来说本就阴云密布：面临重要考试和学生会工作的压力，难以结交新朋友，而这个坏消息无疑是雪上加霜。

In those days, I was soaked in depression and a kind of nameless anger, just like Burr after he got disqualified to become the president. All of a sudden, looking at all of those negative feelings, I could understand Burr a bit as a similar wretch. Envy and jealousy are both the poisons that make our hearts ache and scream: “This is so unfair!” It’s impossible to heal the bitter pain for us, and it’s impossible to embrace what it gave us. Just like I said there will be no correct answers to the three questions, all we can do is accept the truth that this feeling always exists in the air transparently. But remember, think before we act when we put our hand on the trigger called envy. 

在那些日子里，我沉浸在沮丧与一种莫名的愤怒之中，就像伯尔失去总统竞选资格后一样。突然之间，看着所有这些负面情绪，我仿佛能理解伯尔这个同病相怜之人了。嫉妒与羡慕都是让我们内心痛苦呐喊的毒药：“这太不公平了！”我们无法治愈这苦涩的伤痛，也无法欣然接受它所带来的一切。正如我所说，那三个问题没有正确答案，我们所能做的就是接受这种感觉如透明的空气般始终存在的事实。但请记住，当我们的手放在名为嫉妒的扳机上时，要三思而后行。

Written By: Hestia Zheng

Title: "What is Schizophrenia? 精神分裂症是什么？"
Text:
"What is Schizophrenia? 精神分裂症是什么？
Image

Eduard Einstein, the son of Albert Einstein, was diagnosed with schizophrenia. The divorce of Eduard’s parents and the disappearance of his father negatively influenced him a lot. Later, Eduard became increasingly withdrawn and suicidal. But what is schizophrenia? Let’s find out.

爱因斯坦的儿子爱德华-爱因斯坦被诊断患有精神分裂症。爱德华父母的离异和父亲的失踪对他 产生了很大的负面影响。后来，爱德华变得越来越孤僻，并有自杀倾向。但什么是精神分裂症呢? 让我们一探究竟。

Image

What does schizophrenia mean? 精神分裂症的定义

Schizophrenia is a mental disorder that has a serious impact on how people think, behave, and feel.

精神分裂症是一种严重影响人们思维、行为和情感的精神障碍。

What are the symptoms of schizophrenia? 精神分裂症的症状

The positive symptoms, the changes in behavior and thinking, include hallucinations, talking in disorganized ways, delusions, and exhibiting inappropriate laughter, tears, or anger. Patients with hallucinations feel, see, taste, or smell things that do not exist in reality. Moreover, patients experiencing delusions do not have a logical thinking. For example, they might think that their family members will harm them.

积极症状指的是行为和思维发生变化了。这包括幻觉、无序的言语、妄想以及不合适的笑声、哭 泣或愤怒。患有幻觉的患者会感知到、看到、品尝到或闻到现实中不存在的东西。更多的是经历妄 想的患者缺乏逻辑思维。例如，他们可能认为家人会伤害他们。

The negative symptoms of schizophrenia refer to the absence or reduction in normal behavior and emotional expressions. These include toneless voices, a decrease in motivation to aim goals, not interested in past hobbies and social withdrawal.

消极症状指的是正常行为和情感表达的缺失或减少。这些症状包括缺乏语调的声音、减少对目标 的动机、不再对过去的爱好感兴趣以及社交退缩。

What does the brain structure of patients appear to be? 分析精神分裂症患者的大脑结构 

A low activity in frontal lobe: Frontal lobe is basically a brain region that helps us to plan, reason, and solve problems. Brain scans indicates that there is an abnormal low activity in the frontal lobes of patients.

前额叶活动低下: 前额叶是大脑中帮助我们计划、推理和解决问题的区域。脑部扫描显示，精神分 裂症患者的前额叶活动异常低下。 

Extremely active in thalamus and amygdala: A study uses PET scan, measuring changes in metabolic processes, and in physiological processes, while patients were hallucinating. The result illustrates that when they saw or heard something, two brain regions became significantly active. One of these areas is thalamus, the site where incoming sensory signal is filtered. The other one is amygdala, the fear processing area.

丘脑和杏仁核过度活跃: 一项研究使用正电子发射断层扫描(PET扫描)测量患者出现幻觉时代谢 过程和生理过程的变化。结果表明，当他们看到或听到某些东西时，两个大脑区域变得显著活 跃。一个是丘脑，这是过滤传入感官信号的区域;另一个是杏仁核，负责处理恐惧情绪的区域。

Image

What are the risk factors for schizophrenia? 精神分裂症的风险因素

Genetics: Much research showed that if a person has schizophrenia, the chance of its offspring developing schizophrenia will increase. For example, the probability of people being diagnosed by schizophrenia is 1 over 100, but if their sibling or parent has the disorder, the probability increases to 1 over 10.

遗传因素: 大量研究表明，如果一个人患有精神分裂症，那么他的后代患病的几率会增加。例如， 精神分裂症的发病概率为百分之一，但如果他们的兄弟姐妹或父母患有此病，患病的概率会增加 到十分之一。 

Environmental: A research suggests that the combination of genes, environments, and life experience can lead to developing schizophrenia. These environmental factors include living in poverty, dangerous, or stressful surroundings, a lack of nutrition before birth, and exposure to viruses.

环境因素: 研究表明，基因、环境和生活经历的结合可能会导致精神分裂症的发生。这些环境因素 包括贫困、危险或压力大的环境、出生前营养不足以及病毒的暴露。

Image

All in all, my initial intention is to let people know more about schizophrenia and care for the misfortunate. Some of them were born to have it, and others had severe past experience. They had no choice. Thus, we should lend a helping hand towards them. Although social support cannot cure schizophrenia, it can help to manage patients’ symptoms.

总的来说，我的初衷是让人们更多地了解精神分裂症并关爱那些不幸的患者。有些人天生就患有 这种疾病，另一些人则是由于过去经历了严重的创伤而患病，他们没有选择。因此，我们应该向 他们伸出援助之手。尽管社会支持无法治愈精神分裂症，但它可以帮助管理患者的症状。

Title: "2025: New Year, New Start"
Text:
"2025: New Year, New Start
Image

With only a few hours left till 2024 comes to an end, I can’t help but reflect on how much I’ve grown over the past year. Transforming from a sophomore into a junior in high school is no joke—it’s been a year of challenges, countless lessons, and, of course, tears. I’ve encountered situations I never expected which led to self-discovery and gave me a clearer vision of the person I aspire to become. The journey hasn’t always been smooth, but it’s been undeniably transformative.

距离2024年结束只剩下几个小时了，我不禁开始回想这一年自己成长了多少：从高二步入高三的这一年充满了挑战，也带来了无数的教训，甚至不少的眼泪。我遇到了许多从未预料过的情况，但也正是这些经历，让我对自己有了更深的了解，让我更加清晰地看到了自己想成为的样子。这段旅程并不总是一帆风顺，却是一次彻彻底底自我改变的经历。

High school often feels like a race to the future—career planning, endless to-do lists, and preparation for college applications. But, I’ve come to realize that these years are fleeting and there’s beauty in the little moments: laughing with friends in the hallways, staying up late to perfect a project, or even the quiet satisfaction of accomplishing a goal. These moments, though small, are the ones I’ll carry with me long after high school ends. They remind me to slow down and cherish the present rather than constantly rushing toward what’s next.

高中生活就像是一场奔向未来的比赛——未来的规划、无尽的任务清单、还有大学申请的准备。但就在这样忙碌的一年里，我逐渐意识到，高中的时间转瞬即逝，而其中的美好往往藏在那些细碎的瞬间里：在走廊里和朋友们笑成一团；为了完成一个项目而熬夜到很晚；更别提达成目标后的那一刻，内心中的小小满足。这些看似微不足道的瞬间，都是我在高中毕业后将珍藏的记忆。它们让我懂得放慢脚步，珍惜当下，而不是一味地向前赶路而已。

Image

A major lesson I’ve learned this year is resilience. It hasn’t been easy, there were those moments of failure and frustration—a poor test grade, things that didn’t go as planned, or times of self-doubt. One moment stands out vividly: preparing for my Chemistry mock exam. I remember sitting at my desk, tears streaming down my face as I tried to focus. My notes were sprawled across the table and tissues piled up as I wiped away the frustration. Looking back, it was in that moment of vulnerability and persistence that I truly understood what resilience means. It’s not about never falling but about finding the strength to get back up each time. Resilience has become a cornerstone of how I approach challenges, reminding me that growth often comes from pushing through discomfort.

具体来说，这一年我学到的一个重要课题是——韧性。生活并不总是轻松的，失败时常发生，就比如那些搞砸了考试，计划被打乱，以及自我怀疑的时刻。对我来说，最让我记忆犹新的一个画面是复习化学模拟考试的时候——那时我坐在书桌前，眼泪不停地往下掉，即使努力让自己集中精神，把笔记摊得满桌都是，纸巾在手旁堆成一座小山，却仍抹不掉我的沮丧。然而，正是那一刻的脆弱，与随后的坚持，让我真正明白了何为韧性。它并不是永不跌倒，而是每次跌倒后，都能找到站起来的力量。这种品质已然成为我面对挑战时的重要支撑，也让我明白，成长往往来自于一步一步地走出那些布满阴云的时刻——纵使多么缓慢。

As the calendar turns and a new year begins, many of us start with New Year’s resolutions—a tradition tied to the hope of starting fresh and making meaningful changes in the new year. In Business class, I learned that effective goals should be SMART:

随着日历翻到新的一年，很多人都会制定新年计划——希望在新的一年里有一个崭新的开始，做出有意义的改变。而在商务课上，我学到了一种制定有效目标的方法，它叫SMART，我在这里推荐给大家：

1. Specific (具体的)

2. Measurable (可度量的)

3. Achievable (可执行的)

4. Relevant (有关联的)

5. Time-bound (有时限的)

Image

While it’s easy to set lofty resolutions, the key is to break them into smaller, actionable steps. For example, instead of saying, “I want to get into my dream college,” focus on the smaller goals that will lead you there—improving your grades by participating more actively in class or exploring extracurricular activities you enjoy. Achieving these smaller steps not only builds momentum but also gives you the confidence to tackle larger challenges.

虽然制定远大的目标听起来很美好，但关键其实在于把这些目标分解成更小的、可执行的步骤。与其说“我要考上梦想的大学，”不如专注于实现一些更小的目标——比如通过更积极地参与课堂来提高成绩，或者探索自己感兴趣的课外活动。这些小目标不仅能帮助我们积累前进的动力，还能提升自信心，以支持我们完成进一步的挑战。

It’s essential not only to set goals but also to create an actionable plan. The journey from where I am now to where I want to be might seem daunting, but breaking down the bigger picture into small, manageable tasks makes it feel achievable. It’s like building a house, one brick at a time, with each brick representing a small step toward a larger vision.

目标需要行动计划的支持，而我们不妨试试，把当下与想象中的未来之间的距离看作一栋房子。这栋房子的整体可能令人望而生畏，但如果将其分解为一块块砖的堆砌，一切似乎就变得可行多了。每块小小的石砖，都是通向那远大目标不可或缺的一步。

Image

As I focus on the small goals and progress I make, I know that challenges will inevitably arise. It’s during tough times that I need to tap into the resilience I’ve been building. In 2024, I learned that failure isn’t a reflection of my worth but an opportunity to grow. In 2025, I plan to embrace setbacks as part of the learning process. When things don’t go as planned, I’ll remind myself to pause, reflect, and reset. I’ll ask, “What can I learn from this?” and use those lessons to fuel my next steps forward.

当然，在专注于小目标和进步的过程中，困境与挫败也是不可避免的。在过去的2024年中，我学到了失败不是对自我价值的否定，而是一个成长的机会。而在2025年，我计划把失败看作学习过程的一部分。当事情不如意时，我会提醒自己停下来反思，然后再次从头开始，并问问自己：“我能从这次失败中学到什么？”——这个问题的答案，往往就是能够推动自己迈出下一步的重要支持。

If you find yourself unsure of where to begin or how to move forward, try this: take one small step today—something simple, like writing down one thing you’d like to improve, organizing your notes, or even just setting aside five minutes to breathe. Sometimes, progress is about small actions you can manage in the moment.

如果在即将到来的新年，你不知道从哪里开始，或者不知道如何前进，也可以试试这个方法：在今天，当下这个时刻，迈出前进的一小步，或者说，做一件简单的事情——比如写下一个你想提高的地方，整理一下笔记，甚至只是抽出五分钟深呼吸。很多时候，前进的契机就藏在那些你立刻就能做到的小小举动中。

2025 is a year of possibilities, and I will continue to write my story. This year is about growth, not perfection; action, not hesitation. A “new year, new start” is my chance to align who I am now with who I want to become, knowing that every moment I invest in myself shapes the person I’m becoming.

我相信，2025年会是充满可能性的一年，而我将继续书写属于自己的故事。这一年，我将追求成长，而非完美；行动，而非犹豫不决。“新的一年，新的开始”是我对成为更好的自己的承诺——这每一个投入到自我成长的瞬间，都将塑造未来我的模样。

Title: "January 2025 Book and Movie/Film Recommendations"
Text:
"January 2025 Book and Movie/Film Recommendations
Image

Happy New Year, Polarity welcomes you to January 2025! We’re thrilled to continue our monthly book and film review series, encouraging everyone to explore new narratives that expands understanding and sparks creativity. Here’s to a year of engaging content and thoughtful discussions—let’s make 2025 a year of discovery and growth!

Book/s Recommendation

The Fault in Our Stars by John Green

Image

The Fault in Our Stars is a deeply emotional young adult novel that explores the themes of love, mortality and the meaning of life. The story is narrated by a 17-year-old girl, Hazel Grace Lancaster, who has been living with terminal thyroid cancer that has metastasized to her lungs. She manages her illness with humor but knowing that the illness is bringing her closer to death, she struggles to make close connections with others as it may leave a painful legacy for those who care about her.

Little did she know her life takes an unexpected turn when she meets Augustus Gus Waters, a charming and optimistic 17-year-old boy who has a touch of osteosarcoma and lost a leg. As the story goes, they form a close bond over the shared struggles of cancer and their love for literature. They both embark on a journey to Amsterdam to find the author of “An Imperial Affliction”, Peter Van Houten, as Hazel desperately wants to know what happens at the end of the book. The trip is also where Hazel and Augustus start building their relationship.

By blending in the elements of humor, the novel explores how love can bring joy, even when facing difficult challenges or circumstances. It reminds readers to cherish the moments in life, no matter if there are imperfections. The measure of a “happy” life is not by length but by embracing the moments of connection, laughter and understanding that gives life meaning. Through the author’s raw and honest portrayal of patients with cancer, “The Fault in Our Stars” teaches readers the importance of knowing and exploring "What is the meaning of life?" "What is love?," but no matter what challenges you face during this “journey”, make every connection and experience count.

A Dog's Purpose by W. Bruce Cameron
Image

A Dog's Purpose is a heartwarming story that follows a dog through several reincarnations with his owner, exploring the meaning of his existence as he forms deep bonds with different owners experiencing a wide range of lives. The story centres on the dog’s connection with a boy named Ethan and his family, as the dog is reborn into different breeds, each time growing closer to Ethan throughout his life. Readers would be able to witness and experience Ethan's life, from his childhood to his adulthood and success.

More than just the tale of a dog’s life, A Dog's Purpose explores the dog’s journey to understand human emotions and the true nature of his existence. In each of his lives, the dog strives to find his purpose while enriching the lives of the people he loves.

The dog’s unwavering faith in love and friendship shows the powerful, timeless connection between humans and their pets. Our pets cannot speak, but this story gently reminds readers of the of the quiet promises out pets make—to offer unconditional love, companionship, and loyalty, not only throughout their lives but, in some way, even beyond.

This story is incredibly soothing, heartwarming, and inspiring. Bailey's unwavering confidence and dedication, his ability to stay true to his purpose despite the numerous challenges he faces, offer a powerful reminder to never give up. Through this book, a valuable life lesson emerges: hold on to your dreams and persist, no matter the obstacles encountered. For anyone feeling unmotivated, struggling, stressed, or down, this story serves as a source of encouragement and strength, helping to navigate through difficult times.

The Hate of Women by Ueno Chizuko
Image

The Hate of Women by Ueno Chizuko is a book that provides a deep and detailed analysis of the challenges faced by women in modern society. This classic work is suitable for anyone interested in gender equality and social culture.

In the book, Ueno Chizuko employs a sharp and insightful approach to analyze the concept of misogyny from various perspectives and levels. Misogyny is presented as a cultural phenomenon prevalent in patriarchal societies, reflected not only in men's discrimination against women but also in women's self-denial. Ueno Chizuko discusses the issue from historical, social, and cultural angles, uncovering the deeper logic behind the phenomenon of misogyny.

Reading The Hate of Women offers a deeper understanding of women's position and struggles in society. The book provides a detailed analysis of the various issues women face, such as the constraints of traditional family values on women and gender discrimination in the workplace, giving readers a clearer insight into women's circumstances.

However, The Hate of Women is a purely theoretical work, and it may not engage readers in the same way as a novel. At times, it can feel somewhat dry. Yet, once immersed in the text, the profound ideas expressed by Ueno Chizuko are striking. Some of the concepts are deep, and certain sentences may require rereading to fully understand. Nevertheless, The Hate of Women is an outstanding sociological work, filled with unique perspectives and refreshing insights. After reading the book, the challenges discussed become more apparent—issues that are encountered in real life. Although the book focuses on Japanese society, its content remains relevant to the social realities in China. It is undeniably worth reading.

This book also provokes thought on gender equality. Through the analysis of misogyny, Ueno Chizuko calls for the dismantling of gender stereotypes and advocates for a fairer, more inclusive social environment.

The Hate of Women is a work of profound intellectual depth and social significance. It offers a unique perspective that reveals the truth behind gender inequality. For those seeking a deeper understanding of women's position in society and issues of gender equality, The Hate of Women is definitely worth reading!

Movie/s and Film/s Recommendation

The Seventh Seal

Image

The Seventh Seal was directed by Ingmar Bergman in 1957. A Swedish film set during the Plague in medieval Europe. A disillusioned knight, Antonius Block, returns from the Crusades who encounters “Death” personified. 

Death in this film is a character thus a name. In an attempt to delay his fate, Block challenges Death to a game of chess. During the game, the knight reflects on life’s meaning; mortality, fate, faith while traversing through a plague-ridden landscape. The knight then meets various characters including a group of traveling performers, a cynical squire and innocent villagers symbolizing different attitudes towards existence and human condition. 

From this classic film, lessons are taught upon us. The inevitability of death, death is an inescapable part of life its just the about the time left till it arrives, Antonius’s chess games symbolizes humanity’s struggle to delay or deny this inevitable truth. Secondly, is the search for meaning. Through Blocks existential crisis , the film explores deep philosophical questions about faith, existence and the search for meaning in a seemingly indifferent world. 

Lastly, the value of compassion and innocence. Simple acts of kindness and purity in certain characters are presented as sources of true meaning and hope amidst chaos. The Seventh Seal remains a powerful meditation on the mortality and the eternal quest for purpose.

Love Actually 

Image

This film is regarded by many as a Christmas must-have. It may not have the dramatic ups and downs typical of other movies because its plot is fragmented with multiple storylines, which might feel a bit scattered and at times, unreasonable. However, by the end, it manages to leave the viewer with a sense of warmth and emotional depth.

Love, as depicted in the film, is an emotion that can be blind and irrational, but it represents something pure, true, and beautiful. When love arrives, the characters in the film become simple, joyful, and passionate. Whether or not the love is reciprocated, its beauty remains undeniable.

The first shot and narration of the film are deeply moving. At the airport, people are seen smiling, kissing, and hugging.

"Whenever there is concern about the state of the world, the immigration gates at Heathrow come to mind. People often think the world is filled with hatred and greed, but this perspective is challenged. It is believed that love is everywhere, though it may not always be full of vigor and vitality, but love will always persist. Father and son, mother and daughter, husband and wife, boyfriend and girlfriend, old friends—when the plane hit the World Trade Center, the deathbed phone call wasn’t about revenge, but about love. Those who look closely will realize that love is all around."

Set in London before Christmas, the film weaves together ten short stories about friendship, affection, and love. While each story is independent, they are also interwoven, showing how lives and emotions are connected in unexpected ways.

One of the most memorable stories is about a father (stepfather) who encourages his son to bravely express his feelings and share his love. This is a story that Chinese parents may relate to, as they often struggle with the so-called "puppy love" of their children. The little boy asks, "Is there anything more serious than love?" Ultimately, he confesses his love to the girl successfully. The courage and joy with which children approach love remind us that as they grow, the warmth of the sun will always follow their hearts.

Title: "玩物丧志吗？Can a Hobby Really Harm Your Success?"
Text:
"玩物丧志吗？Can a Hobby Really Harm Your Success?
Image

一个人过度沉迷于自己的爱好，而忽略了本职工作——我们一般将此行为称为“玩物丧志”。但有些爱好也可以玩出学问，比如这篇文章要介绍的折纸，就有着令人意想不到的作用。

When someone becomes overly obsessed with their hobbies, neglecting their responsibilities, we often label them as "losing ambition to indulgence." But some hobbies can lead to remarkable discoveries. Take origami, for instance—a practice with surprisingly profound applications, as this article will reveal.

什么是折纸？在我们的印象中，折纸是小时候的千纸鹤，玩具，或者东南西北这一类东西。但是这篇文章有可能颠覆你的认知。

To most of us, origami brings to mind childhood crafts like paper cranes, toys, or fortune tellers. But this perception might change entirely after you read this.

事实上，折纸是一门艺术，它可以飞上太空，甚至可以救人一命。

In reality, origami is an art form that can reach outer space and even save lives.

Image

折纸这种技艺已经存在了数百年。18世纪，折纸作为民间文化以人传人的形式在日本繁荣发展。直到20世纪，折纸艺术家创造了图解，这使得折纸可以通过图文的形式广泛传播。

Origami has been practiced for centuries. By the 18th century, it had flourished in Japan as a folk art passed down orally. It wasn’t until the 20th century that origami diagrams were invented, enabling the practice to spread globally through illustrations and texts.

然而，现代的折纸大师已经不满足于让折纸停留在折叠这个限制性的层面。

Modern origami masters, however, refuse to let origami remain confined to the act of folding paper.

一张正方形的纸，没有裁剪，没有粘贴，只有依靠双手的无数次折叠。

A single square sheet of paper—no cutting, no gluing, only countless folds crafted by skilled hands.

Image

以上这些折纸作品来自美国的Robert J Lang。它们看似不可思议，其实只是将数学运用的淋漓尽致。

These intricate works of Robert J. Lang, an American origami artist, may seem impossible, but they demonstrate how amazing mathematics is.

开始接触折纸时，Robert按照书籍上的指导去折。渐渐的，他尝试改进和创新。在这个过程中他经历了无数次失败，但他总会重新拿起一张纸，然后，不断做新的尝试。

When Robert first began folding paper, he followed instructions in books. Over time, he started to innovate, experimenting with new techniques. His journey was filled with countless failures, yet each time, he would pick up another sheet of paper and try again.

多年以来，有人说他“玩物丧志”，有人问他“折纸有什么用？”。然而，这些看似无用的东西，却有着出乎意料的作用。

Over the years, some accused him of “wasting time on frivolities.” Others asked, “What’s the point of your works?” Yet this seemingly pointless pursuit turned out to have astonishing applications.

Image

在工作的百忙之中，他仍然抽出时间坚持他的折纸爱好，更利用折纸技巧解决了生活中的很多实际问题。他协助NASA设计的太阳能板在旅途中折叠到仅有几米，并在太空中的目的地展开。他与一家德国的安全气囊公司合作，运用昆虫足部的折叠方法，解决了如何最大限度压缩气囊的问题。在医学方面，他曾与医药公司合作开发出能进入心脏的微小手术机器人，为手术医生解决了难题。

Amid his busy work life, Robert continued his passion for origami, even using it to solve practical problems. He helped NASA design solar panels that could fold down to a few meters for transport and then unfold in space. He collaborated with a German airbag company to use folding mechanisms that resembles insect legs to optimize airbag compression. In medicine, he worked with pharmaceutical companies to create tiny surgical robots capable of navigating the human heart, offering doctors revolutionary and helpful tools.

同样把折纸术应用到现实生活中的例子，还有一家医疗技术公司开发的可折叠的网状心脏支架，它可以先折叠起来，穿过狭小的空间植入人体，然后再展开形成圆柱形的支架。

Another example of origami-inspired innovation is the development of collapsible, mesh-like heart stents by a medical technology company. These stents can be folded to pass through narrow spaces in the human heart and then expanded into cylindrical shapes to provide support.

这些解决了实际问题的数学算法，最初只是用来完成折纸艺术作品的理论，但它们最终却和科技意外地结合起来。

The mathematical algorithms behind these solutions were initially developed for creating intricate origami art, yet they eventually found their way into groundbreaking technological advancements.

Image

有时候，看似无用的爱好，却有着出乎意料的作用。尽管这很反常识，但是如你所见，折纸甚至可以拯救人们的生命。

Sometimes, hobbies that appear useless can lead to surprising outcomes. As counterintuitive as it may seem, but just like origami — it can even save lives!

有些事情没有所谓的有用和所谓的意义——当你在这件事情上花费了时间，当这件事情丰富了你的人生，它就有了意义。

Meanings of things don’t always depend on wether they have an immediate, tangible benefit. If it brings you joy and enriches your life, then it holds meaning.

很多人说玩物丧志，却忘了玩物亦可养志。所以，你还在坚持你的爱好吗？如果还没有找到一个爱好，那就去寻找吧，去尝试！

While many criticize hobbies as distractions, they often forget that a hobby can also be motivations. So, are you still pursuing your passion? If not, it’s time to start searching and experimenting. Who knows where it might lead you?

Written By: Franny Guo

Title: "Movie Review: Along With the Gods"
Text:
"Movie Review: Along With the Gods
Image

Along With the Gods tells the story of a man who lived as a dedicated firefighter. After his death, he meets 3 gods who serve as his guardians in a series of trials, judged by another group of gods. Despite being known for his good deeds, the man, burdened by past mistakes, does not see himself as a paragon. His life is examined through trials of deceit, indolence, injustice, betrayal, violence, murder, and filial impiety. The gods guide him through these trials, offering him a chance at reincarnation if he succeeds. As the trials unfold, the reasons behind his choices and regrets are revealed. The film explores themes of morality, self-forgiveness, and the complexity of human nature, with the gods playing a crucial role in guiding the man toward redemption, understanding, and a deeper reflection on life’s moral struggles.

《与神同行》讲述了一个尽职尽业的消防员的故事。死后，他遇到了 3 位神，并在之后的试炼中担任他的守护神，但他同时也被别的神审判。尽管他因善举而闻名，但他仍承受着过去罪恶的煎熬，也不认为自己是一个好人。他将通过欺骗、懒惰、不公正、背叛、暴力、谋杀和孝顺的考验，并以此来审视他的一生。众神将会引领他进行这些考验，并在他成功后给予一个轮回的机会。随着审判的开始，他抉择和懊悔背后的原因被揭露。这部电影探讨了有关道德、自我宽恕和人性复杂的主题。而众神在引领人类走向救赎、理解和对人生道德斗争的深入反思中起至关重要的作用。

Image

"I'm a bad person" 

“我是坏人”
- Kim Ja-hong
Sometimes, it’s all too easy for us to judge people. When we see someone do something bad, such as stealing money or cheating on an exam, we immediately assume that since they have committed a crime, they are therefore bad people. But I believe there is no pure good or evil in this world. People may do bad things with good intentions, or even good things with bad intentions. What we see isn’t always everything; there’s always something that goes beyond people’s actions. The movie illustrates that the positive value of good intentions can be greater than the harm of bad actions. And the main character’s story unfolds like that. He is first presented as a paragon, someone who has done many good deeds in life, yet he never considered himself as one. 

有时，我们会太过片面地去评价一个人。当我们看到有人在做坏事，如盗窃财务或考试作弊时，回想当然地把他们假设为既定犯，并定义为坏人。但我相信这并不是一个非黑即白，正邪不两立的世界。人们可能会好心办坏事；或者想做坏事却适得其反。我们所看见的并不总时全部；人们的行为总有一些引申意。这部电影说明了善良的动机可能比恶来的更加可怕。主角的故事便是如此展开。他最初被认为是个一生中做过许多好事的好人，可他自己却从不这么认为。

Image

"I didn't want to be a hero. I just wanted to do what I had to do."

“我不想成为救赎，我只是想尽我的应尽之责。”
- Kim Ja-hong

As the trials progress, we learn more about the life he lived and the kind of person he truly is. Each trial reveals his sins, leading us to believe that he has done many bad things, but what makes him different from the true sinners is that he had good intentions for all the bad things he has done. The judges of the trials were quick to assume that because he did something bad, he should be punished for it. But his guardians defend him by revealing his reasons, intentions, and positive outcomes of what seemed to be bad. It interestingly discusses issues such as life choices and their outcomes. The life of the main character unfolds as he progresses through each trial, revealing to us why he thinks so badly of himself and why he should forgive himself, further proving that he really is a good person.

随着审判的进行，我们逐渐揭开他的生活和他真正的身份。每一次试炼都揭示了他的罪，也让我们相信他犯下了许多罪恶，但把他与真正的罪人区分开来的是，他所有罪恶的起源都是善意。审判的法官很快便下定了结论，他坏事做尽，他因受惩罚。但他的守护神通过展示这些罪恶背后的原因、意图和积极的结果来为他辩护。它有趣地讨论了有关人生的选择及最终的结果。主角的一生随着每次审判的进展而展开，向我们阐明了他持续批判自己的和应宽恕自己原因，也进一步证明他真的是一个好人。

Image

"It's not about being a good person or a bad person. It's about whether you understand your own actions."

“这并不在于成为一个好人或坏人，而在于与自己行为和解。”
- Gangrim (the cheif guardian god)

This movie made me look back on my life and the choices I’ve made throughout my journey. The trials the main character went through also reminded me of the sins I have committed in my life. It made me feel bad, regret my actions, and blame myself for the things I have done. But at the end of the movie, I realized that the purpose of the trials isn’t to punish or to remind us of our sins, but to give us a chance to repent and seek redemption for what we have done. It gives us a chance to defend ourselves and find value in the good things we have done. Sometimes, we may think that we aren’t a good person and that we may not be living a good life. But this movie has served as a reminder to forgive ourselves the way we forgive others. Because our bad deeds don’t define us, they may just be masks of our good intentions. Although people don’t see these good intentions, as long as we keep them in mind, we can forgive ourselves and move on with our lives.

这部电影让我回忆起了自己的一生和在这场旅途中做出的选择。主角所经历的考验也让我回忆起了一生中所犯下的罪恶。这让我感觉很糟糕，也对自己的行为感到懊悔和自责。但在电影的结尾，我意识到试炼的目的不是为了惩罚或提醒我们的罪，而是给我们一个机会来悔改并为我们所做的一切寻求救赎。它让我们有机会保护自己，并从我们的善举汲取价值。有时，我们可能会认为我们不是一个好人，我们可能不应有好的一生。但这部电影提醒我们在恕人的同时，也应恕己。罪恶并不应束缚我们，那这只是我们善意的面具。虽然这些善意并不被察觉，但只要我们牢记它们，便可以原谅自己并继续生活。

Image

"You must face your sins, but you must also acknowledge the good you've done. It's the only way to move forward."

“你应直面你的罪恶，也应承认你的善举。这是前行的唯一途径。”

- Gangrim (the chief guardian god)
Another theme that this movie highlighted was the importance of expressing feelings, especially to our family. Our traditional culture and society make us used to keeping our deepest thoughts and feelings from our loved ones when they’re the ones we’re supposed to share them with. Because we “love them so much,” we don’t want them to worry or care too much about us.  But in fact, what we need from each other isn’t protection from the truth, but the truest form of our feelings. Only deep communication with our family brings us together and ties us for a lifetime. 

这部电影所强调的另一个主题是情感表达的重要性，尤其是对我们的家庭。我们的传统文化和社会，让我们习惯于将本该与最深切的亲人分享的想法和感受深埋于心。因为我们 “爱之深”，所以不希望他们的“心之切”。 但事实上，我们并不应该屏蔽自己的真实想法，而应展示我们最真实的情感。只有与家人深入交流，才能让我们走到一起，联系在一起。

Image

"I'm sorry I didn't tell you how much I loved you. I thought you would understand."

"很抱歉没有告诉你，我有多爱你。我以为你会明白。”
- Kim Ja-hong's father
Recently I’ve learned from an experience the importance of “沟通”. Although our emotions drive us to run away from situations and pretend nothing happened, it’s actually easier to express our concerns and communicate our way to finding solutions to the problem. Running away doesn’t change anything, and keeping quiet worsens the situation. We should all learn to take some time to talk to our loved ones and express our true feelings and concerns, further strengthening our bonds and showing our love for them.

最近，我从一次经历中学到了“沟通”的重要性。尽管我们的情绪驱使着我们逃避各种问题并假装无事发生，但实际上通过表达我们的担忧并传达我们正在寻找问题的解决方案会是一个更简单的方法。逃跑并不会改变任何事情，保持沉默会只使情况恶化。我们都应该学会花一些时间与我们所爱的人交谈，表达我们的真实感受和担忧，进一步加强我们的联系并表达我们对他们的爱。

I really hope you can watch this movie with your family, as you all watch the slow reveal of the main character’s backstory. The beginning of the movie will make you look back on your life and experiences, and each trial will remind you of your choices and their consequences. The end will make you recall your memories with your family, highlighting a meaningful life. After watching the movie, I hope you can express your deepest thoughts and feelings about the movie with your family. Let them know how you feel after watching it, and express to them how much you love them. Because our life isn’t a movie that ends after the credits, it goes on as long as we live. This movie shows us how life, in general, is too short for us to hold on to sins and escape harmful situations, but it is long enough for us to redeem ourselves and express our love to our loved ones.

我真诚的希望你能和家人一起看这部电影，你们都将看着主角背景故事的被慢慢揭示。电影的开头会让你回顾自己的一生和过往，每一次审判都会让你审视自己的抉择和后果。结尾会让你回想起与家人的记忆，突显生活的意义。看完电影后，希望你能和家人一起表达你对这部电影最深切的想法和感受。让他们知道你看完后的想法，向他们表达你有多爱他们。因为我们的生活并不是一部在演职员表之后就结束的电影，只要我们还活着，它就会继续。这部电影向我们说明了，生命之短，短到我们无法承受罪恶和逃避的后果；生命之长，长到让我们可以自我救赎并向所爱之人表达我们的爱意。

Written By: Jamila Gapuz

Title: "不管宇航员再聪明，到了太空都会变笨?"
Text:
"不管宇航员再聪明，到了太空都会变笨？
Image

许多进入太空的宇航员都是地球上最聪明的人。然而，美国国家航空航天局的一项新研究发现了太空旅行的一个令人惊讶的影响——它实际上可能会减慢人类大脑的速度。与你所期望的相反，研究人员发现，当太空旅行者绕地球运行时，他们会经历一些暂时的思维减速，包括处理信息的速度变慢，注意力和记忆力出现困难。

Many astronauts who venture into space are among the brightest minds on Earth. However, a surprising finding from NASA’s latest research suggests that space travel might actually slow down brain function. Contrary to expectations, researchers discovered that space travelers experience temporary cognitive slowdowns while orbiting Earth. These include slower information processing, difficulties with attention, and memory lapses.

幸运的是，这项研究还发现，在太空中呆上几个月并不会永久性地扰乱宇航员的认知能力。他们的整体大脑表现仍然非常有弹性。这项研究调查了25名专业宇航员，他们平均在国际空间站（ISS）呆了6个月。科学家们通过一系列严格的测试来追踪他们的认知表现，这些测试旨在衡量从处理速度到记忆力和注意力的一切。

The good news? Spending months in space doesn’t cause permanent damage to astronauts’ cognitive abilities. Their overall brain performance remains remarkably resilient. The study involved 25 professional astronauts who spent an average of six months aboard the International Space Station (ISS). Scientists tracked their cognitive performance through rigorous tests designed to measure everything from processing speed to memory and attention.

“我们发现，在ISS呆6个月的宇航员没有任何明显的认知障碍或神经退行性衰退的证据，”该研究的首席研究员希娜德夫博士在一次媒体发布会上解释说。

Dr. Sinead Dev, the study’s lead researcher, explained during a media briefing: “We found no evidence of significant cognitive impairment or neurodegenerative decline in astronauts after spending six months on the ISS.”

那么到底发生了什么变化呢？你可以把它想象成你的大脑在“低功耗模式”下运行。宇航员完成任务的准确度和在地球上一样，但他们处理信息的时间稍长一些。处理速度、工作记忆和注意力是受影响最大的认知领域——类似于你在压力大、睡眠不足的一天后的感觉。

Imagine your brain operating in “low-power mode.” While astronauts maintain the same accuracy when completing tasks as they do on Earth, they take slightly longer to process information. The most affected cognitive areas include processing speed, working memory, and attention—similar to how you might feel after a stressful, sleepless day.

最有趣的发现是大脑适应的速度有多快。一些表现变化，比如注意力持续时间变慢，只有在任务初期才会被注意到。其他一些变化，比如处理速度下降，在宇航员返回地球后需要更长的时间才能恢复正常。

Interestingly, the brain’s adaptability is striking. Some changes, like slower attention spans, were only noticeable during the initial stages of a mission. Other changes, such as reduced processing speed, took longer to return to normal after astronauts returned to Earth.

这些见解不仅仅是科学上的好奇心。随着人类将目光投降雄心勃勃的月球和火星任务，了解人类大脑如何对极端环境作出反应变得至关重要。这项研究为未来的太空探险者提供了一个基线，帮助任务规划者预测和减轻潜在的认知挑战。

These findings are more than a scientific curiosity. As humanity sets its sights on ambitious lunar and Martian missions, understanding how the human brain responds to extreme environments becomes critical. This research provides a baseline to help mission planners anticipate and mitigate potential cognitive challenges.

德夫博士指出了一个重要的警告：这项研究并没有调查这些轻微的认知变化是否正的影响了宇航员在太空中完成工作的能力。研究人员说：“即使在观察到认知能力下降的地区，宇航员仍然能够补偿并有效的完成任务。”

Dr. Dev emphasized a crucial point: the study didn’t assess whether these minor cognitive changes impacted astronauts’ ability to perform their duties. She noted: “Even in areas where cognitive decline was observed, astronauts were able to compensate and complete their tasks effectively.”

这项研究突出了人类大脑令人难以置信的适应性。尽管辐射、重力改变、睡眠中断，以及生活在离家数百英里的密闭空间中的心理压力，我们的认知能力仍然非常稳定。

Despite the radiation, altered gravity, disrupted sleep, and psychological stress of living hundreds of miles away from home in confined spaces, our cognitive abilities remain astonishingly stable.

对于有抱负的宇航员和太空爱好者来说，传递的信息是明确的：人类的大脑比我们想象的要有弹性得多。我们的大脑可以适应看起来完全陌生的环境，即使被推到非同寻常的极限，它也能以令人印象深刻的精度继续运作。

For aspiring astronauts and space enthusiasts, the takeaway is clear: the human brain is far more resilient than we imagine. It can adapt to environments that seem entirely alien, maintaining impressive functionality even when pushed to extraordinary limits.

Written By: Christine Liu

Title: "被优绩主义困住的我们 Trapped by Meritocracy"
Text:
"被优绩主义困住的我们 Trapped by Meritocracy
Image

“你成绩不好就是因为你不够努力。”

"The reason your grades are poor is because you're not working hard enough."

在我的记忆中，这句话几乎伴随了我过去将近一半的人生。如今，“努力”似乎成为了一切问题的答案——“你想获得财富？”“那就去努力吧。”“你希望实现梦想？”“那也去努力吧。”社会承诺我们“只要努力，就能成功。”但这种理想状态下完全公平的竞争几乎不可能存在，我们的家庭背景，生活环境，基因，甚至性别都会成为影响竞争的因素。但如果忽略这一系列的因素，让起点不同的人们奔跑向同一个终点，且根据到达终点的时间来划分阶级与财富，这个比赛注定是不公平的，这个例子就是当代优绩主义的体现。

In my memory, this sentence has accompanied almost half of my life. Nowadays, "effort" seems to be the answer to all problems—"Do you want to achieve wealth?" "Then just work hard." "Do you want to fulfill your dreams?" "Work hard for that too." Society promises us that "as long as you work hard, you will succeed." But this ideal state of completely fair competition is almost impossible to achieve. Our family background, living environment, genes, and even gender all become factors influencing competition. If we ignore these factors and make people with different starting points race toward the same finish line, and then divide the classes and wealth based on the time it takes to reach the finish, this race is destined to be unfair. This example is a reflection of contemporary meritocracy.

Image

优绩主义是指社会与经济的奖赏应当依据才能、努力和成就这些“优绩”来决定。优绩主义在历史进程中，曾经对弱势社会阶层的上升起过巨大的促进作用，并不应该完全作为被批判的对象。而这些“优绩”在当今却转化为了过于僵化的评判标准 ，比如学业成绩。最近浙江大学公众号发表的一篇文章把这个问题推上了风口浪尖，“24/67656，他们拿下浙大最高层次奖学金”—— 一个简单的分数其实也把社会暗流中的阶级关系摆上了台面，竞争固然是残酷的，但其中渐渐消失的人文关怀却是更加可怕的，一颗颗闪耀的星辰却被学校当作那只为了用来衬托的分母，如果我们的价值在优绩主义的系统中被忽视，那我们怎么还有勇气去做梦，去追求自己的梦想呢。

Meritocracy refers to the idea that social and economic rewards should be determined based on talent, effort, and achievement—these "merits." Throughout history, meritocracy has played a significant role in promoting the upward mobility of disadvantaged social classes and should not be entirely dismissed or criticized. However, these "merits" have now transformed into overly rigid standards of evaluation, such as academic performance. A recent article published on Zhejiang University’s official WeChat account brought this issue to the forefront: "24/67656, they won the highest-level scholarship at Zhejiang University." A simple number actually exposes the class relationships lurking beneath the surface of society. While competition is undeniably harsh, what is even more frightening is the gradual disappearance of humanistic concern. Shining stars are treated by the university as mere divisors to serve as a backdrop. If our value is overlooked within the system of meritocracy, how can we still have the courage to dream and pursue our aspirations?

因为这个困扰了我许久的问题，我也询问了我身边的同学对优绩主义的看法，但到最后采访都会陷入某种沉默，与这种体制，或者我更愿意称之为一种处境相比，我们的声音太渺小，我们也不敢用自己的人生作为赌注。但就像所有的自由都是相对的自由，究竟有什么是我们能做的，让身处其中的我们认可自己那不被看到的努力与被束缚住的价值。

Because this troubling issue has been on my mind for quite a while, I asked my classmates about their views on meritocracy. However, the interviews always ended up in a kind of silence. Compared to this system, or what I prefer to call a situation, our voices are too small. We also don’t dare to stake our lives on it. But just like all freedoms are relative, what, in the end, can we do to help us—those who are trapped within this system—recognize our unacknowledged efforts and the value that is constrained?

Image

美国心理学家霍华德加德纳提出了一个“多元智能理论”，他主张将人类智能划分成不同的智力成分，而不是定义为单一的，一般的能力。其实我们每一个人都可以在其中找到自己擅长，或者说比较感兴趣的领域，这就是我们所说的热爱。热爱也许并不能够抵御一切的外界的质疑和自我怀疑，但至少它可以让我们的努力更有方向一点，能让我们更容易看到自己的进步，从而对自己多一点认可和鼓励，让我们看到自己的价值。也许热爱的作用在当下微乎其微，它就像你一直揣在口袋的那颗糖，也许你有时会忽视它的存在，但当你觉得一切都不会变好的时候，它就是那刻彻底的黑暗中中的唯一一点光亮。

American psychologist Howard Gardner proposed the theory of "Multiple Intelligences," suggesting that human intelligence should not be defined as a single, general ability but rather be divided into distinct components. In fact, each of us can find an area in which we excel or, perhaps more accurately, one that we are passionate about. This is what we call love or passion. Passion may not be able to fend off all external doubts and self-doubt, but at the very least, it can give our efforts a sense of direction, making it easier to see our progress and offer ourselves more recognition and encouragement, thus helping us recognize our own value. Perhaps the role of passion seems minimal in today's world; it’s like a piece of candy you keep in your pocket. Sometimes, you may forget it's there. But when you feel that nothing will ever improve, that small piece of candy becomes the only light in the midst of complete darkness.

最后，希望所有人都能心怀自己的热爱，不论在何时何处，不论我们走向的是光明还是黑暗。  

In the end, I hope everyone can carry their passion in their hearts, no matter when or where, whether we are walking towards light or darkness.

Written By: Cathy Zheng

Edited and Translated By: Jenny Huang

Title: "Life is Soup and I’m a Fork"
Text:
"Life is Soup and I’m a Fork
Image

Life is soup. It’s uncontrollable, unpredictable, and sometimes a little too hot to handle. And here I am, a fork, trying to navigate and control the liquid chaos. You may think I’m the wrong tool for the job, but isn’t that the beauty of it? 

生活如汤。它是不可控制的、无法预测的，有时候还会烫得让人难以招架。而我呢，就像一把叉子，试图驾驭并控制这片液体的混乱。你可能会觉得，我是个不适合的工具，但这不正是它的美妙之处吗？

Have you ever tried eating soup with a fork? If not, you can probably imagine how absurd and frustrating it would be. You can only do so much with the fork as it struggles to scoop the soup and spills the liquid everywhere. Similarly, we often try to control what’s inherently uncontrollable, attempting to fix messy situations because we think we can get them under control. 

你有没有试过用叉子喝汤？如果没有，你可能可以想象那会有多荒唐和让人沮丧。一把叉子能做的很有限，它努力想舀起汤，却总是洒得到处都是。同样地，我们经常试图控制那些本质上无法控制的事物，试图去修复混乱的状况，因为我们以为自己能够掌控一切。

Image

Life has a way of throwing unexpected challenges at us. We make plans, set goals, and expect a smooth, easy path, but like a bowl of soup, life is rarely stable and perfect. It’s messy, emotional, and full of surprises. Some days it’s hot, other days cold, sometimes too salty, and occasionally too bland. No amount of planning can change that, and that’s just the nature of life.

生活总是会向我们抛来意想不到的挑战。我们制定计划，设定目标，期待一条顺畅、平坦的道路，但生活就像一碗汤，几乎从不稳定或完美。它是混乱的，情绪化的，充满了意外。有时是热的，有时是冷的，有时太咸，有时又太淡。再多的计划都无法改变这一点，而这正是生活的本质。

Even though chaos and unpredictability are natural, we still try to impose control. We stick to rigid schedules, strive to maintain a flawless image, and meticulously plan every move in an effort to achieve perfection. We convince ourselves that if we make enough decisions, plan enough steps and control enough variables, we can master everything. But in doing so, we miss the entire point.

即便混乱和不可预测是自然的，我们仍然试图强加控制。我们坚持严格的日程安排，努力维持完美的形象，精心计划每一步，力求达到完美。我们相信，如果做出足够多的决定，规划足够多的步骤，并控制足够多的变量，就可以掌控一切。但这样做的结果，是让我们错过了生活的真谛。

Image

The more we try to control every detail, every variable, and every event, the more we strip away the richness of life. There is something beautiful about life’s messiness and simply existing within it. When we stop trying to control everything, we allow space for impulsiveness, growth, and even failure. It is through the mess that we learn, adapt, and build resilience. By letting go of our need for control, we open ourselves to experiencing life as it truly is, not how we wish it would be or could have been. 

我们越是试图控制每个细节、每个变量、每个事件，就越是剥夺了生活的丰富多彩。生活的混乱和仅仅存在其中本身就是一种美。当我们停止尝试控制一切时，就为冲动、成长，甚至失败留下了空间。正是在混乱中，我们学会了适应、成长，并建立起韧性。当我们放下对控制的执念时，我们才能真正地体验生活，感受到它的本来面貌，而不是它应该是或我们希望它成为的样子。

Finally, the metaphor of using a fork to eat soup is about relinquishing the urge to control every aspect of life. It’s about realizing that sometimes the perfect tool for the job doesn’t exist, leaving us with a choice: fight against the reality of the situation or embrace and learn from it. The real lesson isn’t about making the fork work in the soup. The real lesson is that life, with all its messiness, is perfectly fine as it is. And so are we.

最后，用叉子喝汤的比喻，是关于放弃对生活每个方面的控制欲。这是在提醒我们，有时候根本不存在所谓的完美工具，这让我们面临一个选择：要么与现实对抗，要么接纳并从中学习。真正的意义不在于让叉子在汤中派上用场，而在于明白，生活的混乱和不完美本身就是一种美好。而我们，也一样。

Image

This article was inspired by 'Forky' from Toy Story. Forky started off as an insecure fork who was unsure of his place in life. He struggled to find his purpose as he always thought of himself as 'trash' and repeatedly tried to throw himself away. However, as he faced several challenges and experienced more of life, he began to embrace life and its messiness. He realized he didn't need to perfect or be like the other toys to have value.

这篇文章的灵感来源于《玩具总动员》中的“叉奇”。叉奇一开始是一个不自信的小叉子，对自己在生活中的定位感到迷茫。他总是认为自己是“垃圾”，不断试图把自己丢掉。然而，随着他经历了许多挑战并感受了更多生活的意义，他开始接受生活及其混乱的不完美。他明白了，他不需要变得完美，也不需要像其他玩具一样，才能拥有自己的价值。

Title: "Sleep and Dreams"
Text:
"Sleep and Dreams
Image

Have you ever had an experience that environmental information occurring simultaneously with sleeping relates to your dream content? For instance, if your friends chat while you are sleeping, your dream content might be similar to that scene. In this article, sleep stages, the factors determining sleep content, the question above and the purposes of dreams will be explained.

你是否有过这样的经历，即睡觉时同时出现的环境信息与你的梦境内容有关？例如，如果你的朋友在你睡觉时聊天，你的梦境内容可能会与那个场景相似。本文将解释睡眠阶段、决定睡眠内容的因素、上述问题以及梦的目的。

What stages are included during sleeping? 睡眠包括哪些阶段？

Basically, there are five distinct categories of sleep stages. People who enter the first two stages can be woken easily, while stages 3 and 4 become deeper. The final stage is called “the rapid-eye movement (REM)” sleep. This is when eye movement, low muscle tone, and dreams take place. On the other hand, the first four stages are non-rapid eye movement (non-REM) sleep.

睡眠阶段基本上分为五个不同的类别。进入前两个阶段的人很容易被唤醒，而第三和第四阶段则会变得更加深沉。最后一个阶段被称为 “快速眼动（REM）”睡眠。在这一阶段，眼球运动、低肌肉张力和做梦都会发生。另一方面，前四个阶段为非快速眼动（非快速眼动）睡眠。

When people fall asleep, they enter stage 1 first before moving to stages 2-4. Thereafter, the lighter stages of non-REM sleep reoccur without entering stage 1, and then the REM sleep takes place.

人们入睡时，首先进入第一阶段，然后进入第二至第四阶段。此后，非快速眼动睡眠的较轻阶段会再次出现，但不会进入第 1 阶段，然后进入快速眼动睡眠。

What determines our sleep content? 是什么决定了我们的睡眠内容？

Our dreams tend to be similar to daily activities. For example, after experiencing a trauma, people are likely to have nightmares (Levin and Nielsen, 2007, 2009). More interestingly, our brain continues to track the environment around us while sleeping. This means that sensory stimuli, any environmental information that can be received by senses, and can be responded to, might be involved in our dreams. An example of this is an experiment from Dement and Wolpert 1958. The researchers splashed cold water on participants’ faces, leading them to dreaming about a waterfall. Furthermore, any events that happened 5 minutes before sleeping are lost from memory. This answers why people who awaken briefly cannot remember their dream in the morning.

我们的梦往往与日常活动相似。例如，经历创伤后，人们很可能会做噩梦（莱文和尼尔森，2007 年，2009 年）。更有趣的是，我们的大脑在睡眠时会继续追踪周围的环境。这意味着感官刺激，即任何可以通过感官接收并做出反应的环境信息，都有可能参与我们的梦境。Dement 和 Wolpert 1958 年的一项实验就是一个例子。研究人员向参与者的脸上泼冷水，导致他们梦见瀑布。此外，睡前 5 分钟发生的任何事件都会从记忆中消失。这就解释了为什么短暂惊醒的人在早上记不起自己的梦。

What are the roles of dreams? 梦有哪些作用？

• Consolidating memory: A theory suggested that dreams help to store important memories, while sorting out unimportant memories.

巩固记忆： 一种理论认为，梦有助于储存重要记忆，同时整理不重要的记忆。

• Physiological function: The brain activities during REM sleep develop and preserve our neural pathways.

生理功能： 快速眼动睡眠期间的大脑活动发展并保存了我们的神经通路。

• Dealing threats: Amygdala, the fear processing site, is active during REM sleep. This indicates that dreams may help you to face threats.

应对威胁： 杏仁核是处理恐惧的部位，在快速动眼期睡眠中十分活跃。这表明梦可以帮助你面对威胁。

• Satisfying our wishes.
满足我们的愿望。

Written By: James Chen

Title: "恭喜发财，红包拿来！"
Text:
"恭喜发财，红包拿来！
Image

As the Spring Festival approaches, it’s a great time to revisit the traditions and customs of this important celebration. But how well do we know them?

随着春节的到来，这是一个重温这一重要节日传统与习俗的好时机。但我们对这些习俗了解多少呢？

Most of us know that the date of this special day changes each year, but why? The answer lies in the traditional Chinese calendar, known as the "lunar" or "lunisolar calendar." Chinese New Year's Eve usually falls on the second new moon after the winter solstice. Seeing some unfamiliar terms? Let’s dive into this ancient timekeeping system!

大多数人都知道春节的日期每年都不一样，但为什么会这样呢？答案在于中国传统历法——“阴历”或“阴阳历”。中国农历新年通常落在冬至后的第二个新月。看到一些不熟悉的术语了吗？让我们一起探索这一古老的时间测量系统吧！

Image

The term "lunisolar" means the calendar considers both the moon and sun. The solar cycle is simply the Earth’s orbit around the Sun, marking a "year" (365 days). The moon's cycle defines a "month," representing the period when the moon is between the Earth and the Sun, making it invisible from Earth, roughly every 29.5 days. Therefore, months are 29 or 30 days long, depending on the moon's phases. The first day of the month, or new moon, "Shuo," is when the moon’s dark side faces Earth, and the full moon is "Wang." Therefore, New Year's Eve can fall on the 29th or 30th. Also, a lunar eclipse and a new moon are different! In a lunar eclipse, the moon is in Earth’s shadow. In a new moon, the moon’s dark side faces Earth. During most months, the moon is still slightly visible during these times. This is because of the moon’s 5-degree orbital tilt which doesn’t always allow it to align perfectly with the Sun. So, when the New Year is close, remember to look up at night and see if you can spot the moon!

“阴阳历”这一术语意味着日历同时考虑了月亮和太阳的周期。太阳周期就是地球围绕太阳运行一圈，标志着一个“年”（365天）；而月亮周期定义了一个“月”，即月亮位于地球和太阳之间，从地球上看不到的这段时间，约每29.5天一次。因此，阴阳历的月份为29或30天，取决于月亮的变化——“朔”，即新月，是月亮暗面朝向地球的那天，“望”是满月。因而，除夕夜有时是二十九，有时是三十，虽然通常称为“大年三十”，闽南话中也有“二九夜”的说法。而且，月食和新月是不同的！月食是月亮进入地球的影子，而新月是月亮背向地球的黑暗一面面向地球。在大多数月份中，月亮在这段时间里仍可见一部分，这是因为月亮的轨道有5度倾角，不总是与太阳完美对齐。所以，当新年快到的时候，记得抬头看看夜空，试着找到月亮！

Image

The Chinese calendar is rooted in the theory of Yin and Yang, one of the oldest and most fundamental Chinese philosophies, which suggests that everything in the universe consists of two opposite but complementary forces. It was applied to various aspects of life, ranging from gender to landscape changes, including the calendar. The two solstices—the winter solstice around December 21st, marking the longest night and the shift from Yin (dark and cold) to Yang (light and warmth)—symbolize the balance emphasized in the theory. The ancients believed that combining both the moon (Yin) and the sun (Yang) would produce a reliable calendar.

中国历法的基础是阴阳理论，这是中国最古老、最基本的哲学之一，认为宇宙中的一切由两种对立却又互补的力量组成。这一理论应用于生活的方方面面，从性别到地貌变化，当然也包括历法。冬至——大约在每年12月21日，是一年中夜晚最长的一天，象征着从阴（黑暗与寒冷）到阳（光明与温暖）的转变，体现了阴阳平衡的哲学。古人相信，将月亮（阴）和太阳（阳）结合在一起，可以制定出一个可靠的日历。

Image

Although the winter solstice and new moon are determinants, Chinese New Year doesn’t fall exactly 58 days (2*29.5) after December 21st or 22nd. Instead, it occurs between January 21st and February 20th. This occurs because the lunar year (354 days) is 11 days shorter than the solar year (365 days). To correct this, an extra month called an intercalary month is added every 2-3 years, making Chinese New Year with the longest night in the northern hemisphere, when the sun is directly over the Tropic of Capricorn.

尽管冬至和新月是关键因素，但中国新年并非总是落在12月21日或22日后整整58天（29.5×2）的时候，而是落在1月21日到2月20日之间。这是因为阴历年（354天）比阳历年（365天）短11天。为了调整这差距，每隔2到3年会加入一个闰月，从而使春节与北半球最长的夜晚——太阳直射南回归线的时间一致。

Image

To find the exact date of Spring Festival in the Gregorian calendar, subtract 11 days from the same date in the next solar year. If the result is before January 21st, add 29.5 days for an intercalary month. For example, this year it’s January 29th. Next year, subtract 11 from 29, resulting in 18. Since that’s before January 21st, add 29.5 days, giving us February 17th.

要确定公历中春节的具体日期，可以从下一年的同一天减去11天。如果结果在1月21日之前，则加上29.5天代表一个闰月。例如，今年的春节是1月29日。明年，29减去11等于18。因为1月18早于1月21日，所以再加29.5天，得出2月17日。

But the festival isn’t just about astronomy, history and math—it’s rooted in fascinating legends. We all know the story of Nian, the lion-like monster that raided villages, only to be scared away by red decorations and firecrackers. But where did Nian go after disappearing from sight?

当然了，这个节日不仅仅与天文学、历史和数学有关——它更根植于那些有趣的传说当中。我们都知道“年”，这头凶兽每到新年之夜就会闯入村庄里吃人并大肆破坏，最终人们发现了它的弱点——红色，巨响与火光，并以此赶跑了它，从此它再没出现过。但你有没有好奇过，在这之后，它去了哪里呢？

Image

One version of the myth suggests that it was Hongjun Laozu, the "Great Primal Ancestor," who captured Nian and taught villagers strategies to defeat it. It is said, he came to the village the night before Nian came,  disguised as an old beggar, and hid in the house of an old kind lady who provided him food and shelter. When Nian came, it saw the bright candlelight and red paper decorations on the cottage. Enraged, Nian roared at the house, ripped the paper and smashed the doors, but was met by a laughing elderly with firecrackers in hand. After that, Nian became his companion, following him wherever he went.

有个传说是这样讲的：一年除夕，村民们正要撤出村落以避年之祸乱，却见村外来了个状似乞丐的老人，只见他手拄拐杖，臂搭袋囊，银须飘逸，目若朗星。有位老婆婆好心，给他食物，让他住宿，可她毕竟不相信这位老爷爷能打败年，便也离开了。半夜时分，年闯进村中，却见一片寂静，只有那老婆婆屋内烛火通明，门贴大红纸。年朝那家怒视片刻，随即咆哮着扑过去，这时，那贴满红纸的两扇门大开，只见院内一位身披红袍的老人正哈哈大笑，屋内红烛燃的正旺，竹子炸的满地响。据说，年兽由此就被这位老人收服了，而这位老人就是鸿钧老祖，年兽也并就此成为了他的坐骑。

Image

Hongjun Laozu was no ordinary figure. His name means "the universe before the separation of Heaven and Earth," and he is believed to have created the world from chaos. He is featured in the famous Ming dynasty work Fengshen Yanyi (The Investiture of the Gods), which tells a story involving supernatural beings and humans. Laozu is the eldest of the four beings created by the Spirit of Creation – a very powerful being,  and some even worship him as the "principle behind the universe."

这位鸿钧老祖可是位大人物，他的名字“鸿钧”即“混元”，代表着天地未开、虚空未分之际的宇宙本始状态，传说中更是他将天地从混沌中化来。而鸿钧老祖有文字记载的首次登场，还要属明朝文学作品《封神演义》。在其中，他是太上老君，元始天尊和通天教主的师父，道行深厚，被尊为道祖。

However, Nian isn't the only mythical beast associated with the Spring Festival. Another lesser-known monster, Xi, with green scales and a large thorn, was also scared away by firecrackers. Some say this is why New Year’s Eve is called "Chu Xi" in Chinese, meaning "to eliminate Xi." 

但话又说回来，“年”也并非民间传说中唯一一只会在春节之际跑到人间作乱的怪兽。 除夕夜还有一只一角四足，形貌狰狞，生性凶残，浑身绿盈盈的恶兽——夕，常到附近的村庄里去找吃的。同样，它的弱点与年相同，也因此被逼退。除夕除夕，由此便有了除掉“夕”这只怪兽的意思。

Image

There's also the story of the little ghost Sui with a black body and white hands, who would curse children on New Year’s Eve by patting their foreheads three times while they slept. To prevent this, people would stay awake all night. One family, however, gave their son eight coins wrapped in paper to keep him awake, and it turned out the coins acted as an amulet against Sui! This led to the tradition of giving red packets, or "Ya Sui Qian," which means "money that suppresses Sui."

不仅如此，传说古时候还有个身黑手白的小妖，叫做祟，每年年三十夜里出来，在小孩的头上摸三下，孩子就会生病发烧。人们为了保护自己的孩子，只得点亮灯火熬夜不睡，为“守祟”，后来就传为“守岁”了；后来有一对夫妇想了个法子，为了不让孩子睡觉就用红纸包了八枚铜钱让孩子玩儿，尽管孩子还是睡着了，就在祟要摸他头时，那纸包着的铜币却发出一道金光，祟于是尖叫着逃跑了。后来大家就都效仿开来，用红纸包上八个铜钱给孩子，以祈求平安，这就是“压祟钱”，即“压岁钱”的典故。

Image

So here’s what I want to share with you all: the science behind the date of Chinese New Year, and the mythology passed down through generations by word of mouth. While the former is based on facts, the latter is full of variations, but they’re all stories my grandparents would talk about with great enthusiasm. 

所以，我想和大家分享的是：一方面，春节日期背后的科学；另一方面，那些代代相传的神话传说。前者基于事实，而后者充满了多种版本的变体，但它们都是爷爷奶奶讲得津津乐道的故事

Isn’t it amazing how opposites come together to shape one of the largest celebrations in Chinese culture? Spring Festival has a different meaning to each individual. For example, Baidu and Wikipedia say eating dumplings brings fortune, but my family prefers leek and tofu. While some of you are hanging red couplets today, we did it a week ago. Everything I’ve written here is new to me, so for me, this year’s meaning is about exploring traditions!

对立的两者结合起来，成就了中国文化中最盛大的节日之一，难道不是很神奇吗？春节对每个人来说都有不同的意义。例如，百度和维基百科说吃饺子可以招财，但我家更喜欢吃韭菜豆腐；有人今天贴春联，我们却一周前就贴好了。我写的所有内容对我来说都是新的，所以今年春节的意义对我而言，就是探索传统！

Image

Lastly, I wish everyone a Happy Chinese New Year! 

最后，祝大家新年快乐！

Written By: Grace Cai
