Title: "February 2025 Book and Movie/Film Recommendations"
Text:
"February 2025 Book and Movie/Film Recommendations
Image

Hello, February 2025! A new month means new stories to discover. Whether in the pages of a book or on the big screen, there’s always something to inspire, challenge, and move us. Let’s dive into another month of great books and films!

Book/s Recommendation

The Distant Sunflower Fields by Li Juan

Image

This book chronicles a farming life filled with hardships and unexpected encounters. More like a novel than prose, it captures a fragile yet profound experience of existence—entirely exposed to nature, insignificant yet dignified and full of joy—laid out on the path leading to the sunflower fields.

“Grandma, what kind of dazzling gold is death?” Li Juan writes about her time living with her grandmother, describing their moments together in the sunflower fields.

Under the glow of thousands of acres of sunflowers, summer announces its end, and the grand arrival of autumn begins. Her grandmother, in her lonely admiration, said, “How beautiful it is! Everything is so bright and radiant.” She couldn’t help but wonder again why her grandmother died, why she was willing to leave.

“Grandma, look, the world you gave up remains unchanged. The radiance you loved still arrives on time every year without hesitation.”

“So, Grandma, what kind of dazzling gold is death?” This line left the deepest impression on me. Later, Li Juan’s grandmother moved to the city but never fulfilled her wish to return to Altay. Like many elderly people who have spent their lives in rural areas but are later forced to move to cities to live with their children, her grandmother’s connection to the city was awkward and unfamiliar. This unfamiliarity drew her closer to death.

Death, the final stage of life that the living cannot experience, is imbued with too much meaning by those who remain. For Li Juan, death initially carried a heavy significance: it marked the complete severance of emotional bonds in the physical world. Without her grandmother’s love to rely on, her desires would remain unfulfilled—a reflection of her deep attachment to wanting her loved one to stay. However, for her grandmother, perhaps death was the only way to truly take flight, as she was too old to reintegrate into the world. This kind of suffering directly contradicted the meaning Li Juan assigned to death.

In the end, Li Juan seemed to realize that in her grandmother’s eyes, death might be no different from the golden Altay she adored. Since her grandmother found beauty in it, any attempts at persuasion or retention were ultimately futile.

This book conveys some universal truths to readers, but more often, it simply records the connections Li Juan and her family formed with life and nature. She also depicts the emotional impact of assigning meaning to things, such as her grandmother’s death and her feelings of unbearable shame, as well as the overwhelming awe and transformation she experienced when attributing significance to nature.

In the boundless desert, no answers are visible. Humanity has little choice but to revere and listen to what lies beyond itself and nature.

Stepping out of the role of a reader and returning to my meaning-laden urban life, I feel a sense of relief. Sometimes, I think life is a stagnant pool, perhaps because I’m too caught up in assigning it negative meanings.

You can certainly ponder the meaning of the world and enjoy the pleasure of reflection. But if meaning brings too much pain and fear, don’t forget: We always have the right to ignore its existence.

Contact by Carl Sagan

Image

The novel, “Contact,” by Carl Sagan, is about Ellie Arroway, who decodes a signal from extraterrestrial life. The story explores the tensions between science, politics, and religion, revealing humanity’s intellectual and moral capacity to engage with an advanced civilization.

Dr. Ellie Arroway is a radio astronomer, leading her team, scanning the skies for extraterrestrial signals. After years of relentless efforts, Ellie finally discovers a repeating signal from the Vega star system. The signal contains a series of prime numbers and eventually reveals blueprints for an advanced machine. As nations collaborate and debate construction for this project, conflict arise between scientific communities and political leaders. After the construction of the machine, Ellie becomes one of the individuals to travel through the machine. Her journey through the machine leads to a deeply personal encounter with an alien intelligence who appears as her deceased father. This experience challenged her understanding of life and the universe. However, once she returns back on Earth, there is no physical evidence of her journey and she has to find a way to convince the world of her experience.

This novel shows readers the importance of perseverance. In the novel, Ellie’s determination and the courage to question the uncertainty lead to valuable findings in space exploration even when she is met with skepticism. Her journey reminded me that the pursuit of knowledge is as much about personal growth as it is about discovering universal truths, making me think about the balance between the skepticism and belief in my own life. Most importantly, the way Ellie is portrayed in the novel really inspired me to embrace questioning uncertainties without fear of how others might perceive me because this process is essential for personal growth and development.

The BFG by Roald Dahl

Image

Giants are supposed to eat humans. What happens when a giant chooses not to? Well, that’s what the BFG (Big Friendly Giant) has to go through. Isolated from all the other giants in his cave, the BFG has nothing to eat except giant disgusting snozzcumbers. Not only that, the BFG, being the smallest giant in his group, gets bullied and tossed around whenever he goes out... literally tossed around. While this is definitely enough to make anyone go crazy, the BFG manages to keep his composure with his secret pastime involving a butterfly net and a mysterious giant long trumpet.  Everything changes though, when a little girl manages to make it to giant country alive...

The BFG is a children’s book written by British author Roald Dahl. It tells an interesting, lighthearted story that has fun, unexpected turns in the middle and ends with surprisingly deep lessons. The BFG teaches us that we should stand for what we believe in, just like how the BFG refused to eat humans even it meant being shunned and looked down on by the other giants. It also shows us that sacrifices are still worth it even when it may seem unappreciated at first. Ultimately, the BFG is a great story to read, whether to improve your english or to immerse yourself in the wonderful writing.

Inside Out

Image

Inside Out is a must-watch for teenagers, blending stunning visuals with an emotionally powerful story that highlights the challenges that adolescent face during their puberty time period. The movie also states ways that teenagers could use to address their dramatic change in personality, mood and the way they see things in-terms of relationship with others. 

The movie follows Riley, a 13-year-old girl navigating the emotional turbulence of adolescence. The film captures the confusion, mood swings, and self-doubt that come with growing up, showing how these emotions are not just obstacles, but crucial parts of personal growth. It’s a powerful reminder that it’s okay to feel lost or overwhelmed during this part of time in life and that emotions, even the difficult ones, help shape who we are. The most relating scene in the movie is when audiences hear the phrase “I am not good enough” as it covers all negative emotion including self doubt, self abasement and self accusation. The most vital lesson that could be taken away from the movie is to accept who we are, both the positives and the negatives, because no one is perfect, Riley could be the top student in class, but she can also make silly mistakes; she could play in the hockey school varsity team, but she can also have atypical ideas. 

Inside Out provides valuable insights into coping with life's changes and fostering emotional resilience. It’s a relatable and heartwarming story for anyone navigating the ups and downs of growing up.

Little Women

Image

"Little Women", directed by Greta Gerwig, breathes new life into the classic novel. It's a heartwarming and touching film that I can't wait to recommend to everyone!

The story revolves around the four March sisters. Set in 19th - century New England, they experience life, love, and pursue their dreams. The characters in the movie are incredibly well - portrayed! Jo is a passionate tomboy who dreams of becoming a writer. Watching her grow from a young girl to a renowned author, I seemed to see my own shadow in the pursuit of dreams, and it really resonated with me. Meg, the eldest sister, makes me understand the preciousness of family and the choices between love and wealth. Beth is kind - hearted and gentle. Even when afflicted by illness, she remains selfless, and I couldn't hold back my tears while watching. Amy's transformation from a spoiled girl to a mature woman also deeply touches me.

The film's cinematography is a visual feast. The warm golden hues of the March family home immediately draw me into that loving family. The outdoor scenes of the New England countryside are so beautiful that every frame could be captured as a wallpaper.

Its themes are profound, touching on sisterly bonds, the pursuit of dreams, and the true meaning of love. It reminds me of the unwavering support from my family. No matter how far - fetched our dreams may seem, they are worth striving for.

"Little Women" is not just a movie; it's an unforgettable emotional journey. It's also great for English beginners. Guys, don't miss it and bookmark it right away!
